items.body:
Heads up for anyone whose AV quarantines uv.exe out of the hermes bin folder (C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\hermes\bin\uv.exe).

Bitdefender flags it as Malware.AI.<number>, Defender calls it Trojan:Script/Phonzy.A!ml, a couple other ML engines hit it too. It's a false positive. That exe is Astral's uv, the Rust Python package manager Hermes bundles to manage its Python env. The ML engines trip on it because it's an unsigned Rust binary that goes and installs packages, and there's a pile of upstream reports saying the same thing:

- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/13553
- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/15011
- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/10079

If you want to confirm your own copy before you exclude it, you can. You need the GitHub CLI (winget install --id GitHub.cli, then gh auth login). Then:


$uv  = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\uv.exe"
$ver = (& $uv --version).Split(' ')[1]
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
$zip = "$env:TEMP\uv.zip"
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/$ver/uv-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip" -OutFile $zip -UseBasicParsing
gh attestation verify $zip --repo astral-sh/uv
Expand-Archive $zip "$env:TEMP\uv_x" -Force
(Get-FileHash "$env:TEMP\uv_x\uv.exe").Hash -eq (Get-FileHash $uv).Hash


One thing that'll trip you up: verify the zip, not the loose exe. Running gh attestation verify against the extracted uv.exe gives you a 404. That's not a failure, Astral just attests the release archive, not the unpacked binary. So verify the zip, then the last line checks your exe against the one inside it.

If the attestation says "Verification succeeded" and that last line prints True, you're good. Exclude the folder, not the file hash, since Hermes updates uv and the hash changes every version:


Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin"


Bitdefender users add the exception in the Bitdefender console (Protection > Antivirus > Settings > Manage Exceptions), the Defender command won't touch it.

items.title: [Bug]: openai-codex multi-profile rotation race — rotated grant not written through to global root (Codex analog of #43589)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

This is the **openai-codex analog of #43589** (xAI OAuth). The same multi-profile rotation hazard exists for Codex, and for the same structural reason.

`openai-codex` rotates the `refresh_token` on **every** refresh. Combined with two existing Hermes behaviors, this guarantees grant revocation on any multi-profile install:

1. `_load_provider_state` (hermes_cli/auth.py) falls back read-only to the global-root `auth.json` when a profile has no `providers.openai-codex` entry. Good.
2. But when the credential pool then rotates that grant during a profile session, `CredentialPool._sync_device_code_entry_to_auth_store` writes the rotated chain only into the **profile's** auth store — never back to root.

From that moment root holds a now-revoked refresh token. Every other profile that reads root's stale grant dies with `refresh_token_reused` once its access token expires, and any keepalive refreshing from root fails the same way. Re-auth lands in whichever store the ambient active-profile state points at, seeding a competing chain. With N stores holding refresh tokens for one rotating grant, mutual revocation is a structural certainty, not a race.

## Failure sequence

1. Profile A and Profile B both have no own `providers.openai-codex` block; both resolve the Codex grant from root via fallback.
2. Profile A's access token expires; the pool refreshes. Codex returns a rotated `refresh_token`. The new chain is saved to **Profile A's** store only.
3. Root still holds the old (now revoked) refresh token.
4. Profile B's access token later expires. It refreshes using root's revoked token → `refresh_token_reused`. Profile B is dead until re-auth.

## Expected

A rotated Codex grant resolved from the root fallback should be written **through to root** as well, so the canonical store stays coherent and other profiles reading root keep working — exactly as #43589 fixed for xAI OAuth.

## Actual

The rotated chain is saved only to the active profile store; root keeps a revoked refresh token; sibling profiles die with `refresh_token_reused`.

## Environment

Hermes (current main), macOS, multi-profile install, `openai-codex` via loopback PKCE.

## Related

- #43589 — identical bug + accepted fix for xAI OAuth (write-through to global root). This issue is the Codex equivalent. A fix mirroring that PR follows.

```text
[hermes] Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe; dropping stale connection.
[hermes] [boot] Restarting desktop connection
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[hermes] [boot] Connecting to remote Hermes backend at http://<private-IP>:9119
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend did not become ready: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
```

In another official-auth attempt, logs showed the remote auth state was recognized, but Desktop later fell into local backend startup/onboarding:

```text
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in. Open Settings → Gateway and click "Sign in", or switch back to Local.
...
```

- The remote URL and credentials are valid; the UI reaches `Signed in` before Save/reconnect.
- The remote VM has a configured inference provider. The provider setup screen on Windows appears to be a fallback/local-onboarding artifact, not a real missing remote provider.
- This may be related to remote password-auth gateway session/cookie persistence, WS ticket minting after Save/reconnect, or Desktop liveness probe state being dropped after reconnect.

All passwords/session tokens and private chat details have been omitted.

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

    When using custom_providers pointing to HTTPS endpoints whose certificates are signed
    by a private/corporate root CA, Hermes fails with APIConnectionError because
    _build_keepalive_http_client() in run_agent.py creates an httpx.HTTPTransport
    without a verify= parameter — so it relies on the default certifi bundle, which does
    not include the private CA.

    This is distinct from the existing ssl_verify: false workaround (which disables
    certificate verification entirely, a security regression) and from the global
    HERMES_EXTRA_CA_CERTS env-var approach (PR #24918, which affects all providers in the
    process).

    Affected versions: tested on Hermes v0.14.x (WSL2, Python 3.14.4).

    Concrete case: two custom_providers pointing to internally-hosted Mistral and QWen
    endpoints at https://<internal-host>:30001 and :30002, whose TLS certificates are
    signed by a corporate root CA. The CA cert itself is valid (Basic Constraints: CA:TRUE)
    but lacks the Key Usage extension — which Python 3.14's stricter SSL stack now rejects
    even when SSL_CERT_FILE is set globally, because httpx.HTTPTransport ignores
    SSL_CERT_FILE when a custom transport is provided (httpx design: trust_env applies to
    Client, not to the transport's SSL context).

    Environment

    - OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu on Windows 11)
    - Python: 3.14.4
    - Hermes: v0.14.x (git clone install)
    - Endpoints: internally-hosted OpenAI-compatible inference servers (Mistral, QWen)

### Proposed Solution

    Add an optional ssl_ca_cert field to the custom_providers / providers config entry:

    yaml
    custom_providers:
      - name: My Internal Mistral
        base_url: https://internal-host:30001
        api_key: sk-...
        model: mistralai/Devstral-Small
        ssl_ca_cert: /path/to/my-company-rootCA.crt   # <-- new field


    Behaviour:
    - When ssl_ca_cert is set: pass verify=<path> to httpx.HTTPTransport for that
      provider's keepalive client only. Certificate chain validation is fully maintained
      (no verify=False).
    - When absent: current behaviour unchanged (verify=True, default certifi bundle).
    - Path supports ~ expansion and ${ENV_VAR} substitution (consistent with other
      path fields in config).

    Implementation sketch (two files):

    1. hermes_cli/config.py — add ssl_ca_cert to _KNOWN_KEYS in
       _normalize_custom_provider_entry() and pass it through the normalized dict.

    2. run_agent.py — _build_keepalive_http_client(base_url, ssl_ca_cert=None):

    python
    _ssl_verify = str(pathlib.Path(ssl_ca_cert).expanduser()) if ssl_ca_cert else True
    return _httpx.Client(
        transport=_httpx.HTTPTransport(socket_options=_sock_opts, verify=_ssl_verify),
        proxy=_proxy,
    )


    The caller (agent_runtime_helpers.create_openai_client) already has access to the
    active custom provider entry and can forward the new field.

    Relation to Existing Issues / PRs

    | Reference | Status | What it covers                                                         |
    |-----------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
    | #28260    | Open   | Self-signed cert → proposes ssl_verify: false (turns off verification) |
    | PR #28271 | Open   | Implements ssl_verify globally in _build_keepalive_http_client         |
    | PR #24918 | Open   | HERMES_EXTRA_CA_CERTS — global, process-level extra CA bundle          |
    | #29384    | Open   | Corporate proxy + Gemini; same root cause                              |

    This request is additive and complementary: ssl_ca_cert per-provider with full
    verification maintained, scoped to individual providers rather than the whole process.


### Alternatives Considered

   Alternatives Considered

    - ssl_verify: false per-provider (PR #28271): disables certificate verification —
      not acceptable in a corporate security context.
    - SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable (global): does not propagate to
      httpx.HTTPTransport when a custom transport is supplied (httpx design limitation).
    - Patching _build_keepalive_http_client to read SSL_CERT_FILE (current
      workaround): works but is global, not per-provider; also fails on Python 3.14 when
      the CA cert lacks the Key Usage extension.
    - PR #24918 HERMES_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: good for process-level trust, but cannot
      target a single provider when other providers should use the default bundle.

items.title: [Security] Terminal session snapshots leak .env secrets to disk in plaintext (cache/terminal/hermes-snap-*.sh)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
Bug Description
The terminal persistent-shell snapshot mechanism writes all environment variables — including secrets loaded from .env — to disk in plaintext under cache/terminal/hermes-snap-*.sh. The snapshot file is a full export -p / declare -x dump and is readable by any process or user with filesystem access to HERMES_HOME.

This leaks credentials like API keys, App Secrets, verification tokens, and provider keys. HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS does not protect against this — the redactor only filters tool output before it enters LLM context, not files written directly to disk by shell commands.

Steps to Reproduce
Set any secret in .env — e.g. FEISHU_APP_SECRET=mysecret
Start Hermes and run any terminal command (triggers init_session())
Inspect the snapshot file:
代码
· bash
ls "$HERMES_HOME/cache/terminal/"hermes-snap-*.sh
grep FEISHU_APP_SECRET "$HERMES_HOME/cache/terminal/"hermes-snap-*.sh
Expected Behavior
Snapshot files should either (a) exclude environment variables whose names match known secret patterns, or (b) not be written at all, or (c) be written with restrictive permissions (0600) and cleaned up on exit.

Actual Behavior
Every hermes-snap-*.sh contains the full declare -x output including all .env-sourced secrets. On Windows, these files land in %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\cache\terminal\ and are readable by any process running as the same user. Files persist after Hermes exits — stale snapshots accumulate across sessions.

Example of what's leaked (from a real file):

declare -x FEISHU_APP_ID="cli_xxx" declare -x FEISHU_APP_SECRET="xxx" declare -x FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN="xxx" declare -x DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="xxx"

Root Cause
tools/environments/base.py, init_session() method, around line 373:

代码
· python
bootstrap = (
    f"export -p > {_quoted_snap}\n"   # ← writes ALL env vars, no filtering
    ...
)


`export -p` (bash builtin) prints every exported variable with no
ability to exclude specific names. There is no post-write filtering step
either.

On Windows, `LocalEnvironment.get_temp_dir()` (line 520-533 in
`tools/environments/local.py`) resolves the snapshot directory to
`HERMES_HOME/cache/terminal/` rather than `/tmp`, making the leaked
files persistent and outside typical temp-directory cleanup.

## Possible Fix Directions

1. **Post-write filter**: After writing the snapshot, read it back
   and strip lines whose variable names match the existing secret
   list (or a configurable exclude pattern).

2. **Pre-write filter**: Instead of `export -p > file`, pipe through
   `grep -v -E '^(declare -x (FEISHU_|DEEPSEEK_|OPENAI_|ANTHROPIC_|...))'`
   to exclude known secret-bearing env vars.

3. **Cleanup on exit**: Register `atexit` or `__del__` to remove the
   snapshot files when the terminal session ends.

4. **Restrictive permissions**: At minimum, `chmod 600` the snapshot
   files (though this doesn't help on Windows where NTFS ACLs are
   the relevant mechanism).

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10
- **Hermes version**: latest (git-installed)
- **Terminal backend**: local (`TERMINAL_ENV=local`)
- **Shell**: Git Bash (MINGW64)

## Summary
Desktop can lose its local TUI gateway WebSocket while a long foreground task is streaming output. The running turn continues in the backend, but the renderer sees the gateway as disconnected/reconnecting and the live session is detached from the socket.

## Observed behavior
During long tasks, the backend logs repeated slow writes followed by WebSocket disconnects/resets:

```text
tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:53428 — frame left in flight
ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054] An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host
tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:53428 reason=send_failed_after_response messages=339 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=1 reaped_sessions=0 detached_sessions=1
```

A second earlier connection showed the same close mode:

```text
tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:55591 reason=send_failed_after_response messages=563 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=1 reaped_sessions=0 detached_sessions=1
```

The active process tree at the time included the Desktop dashboard backend and multiple `tui_gateway.slash_worker` processes, including a long-running foreground test command:

```text
python.exe -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
python.exe -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key ... --model gpt-5.5
python.exe -m pytest tests/ -q --maxfail=10 --tb=short -o addopts=
```

## Expected behavior
A long task may stream slowly, but it should not randomly drop the renderer's gateway connection. If the socket does reconnect, the active session should remain attached to the live turn without losing the stream or leaving detached workers behind.

## Suspected area
`tui_gateway/ws.py` writes JSON-RPC frames to a single Starlette WebSocket from multiple caller paths. On loop stalls, `WSTransport.write()` leaves send coroutines in flight. Under long streaming output this can create overlapping `send_text()` calls on the same socket before the event loop catches up, which is a fragile path for Starlette/WebSocket transports.

Relevant code:

- `tui_gateway/ws.py`: `WSTransport.write()` / `_safe_send()`
- `tui_gateway/server.py`: WS disconnect handling detaches sessions via `_close_sessions_for_transport()` and later reattaches through `session.resume`

## Workaround
Run very long/high-output commands as tracked background processes with completion notification, or outside Desktop, to avoid foreground-streaming a large output volume through the TUI gateway socket.

## Environment
- Hermes Desktop on Windows
- Local dashboard backend (`python -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`)
- Main branch observed at `ef4b897a1`

items.title: [Bug] Gateway approval prompts echo unredacted command text, bypassing Tirith's credential redaction

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
Bug Description

When Tirith flags a command for containing a credential-shaped pattern (e.g. credential_in_text / GitHub PAT, OpenAI key), its own finding output is appropriately redacted — it reports that a credential pattern matched, not the matched value. However, the gateway code that turns that finding into a user-facing approval prompt (Telegram, and presumably the other gateway platforms that share this path) builds its message from the raw command string, not the redacted finding. The result: the exact value Tirith just determined should not be disclosed gets sent verbatim to the operator's chat platform anyway, undoing the redaction one layer up.

Environment


Hermes Agent version: v2026.6.5 (verified locally against a clean checkout at this tag)
Also confirmed present in v2026.5.16 (diffed tools/approval.py, tools/tirith_security.py, and the relevant gateway/run.py function against that tag — identical behavior, so this isn't new in this release cycle)
Platform: Telegram gateway adapter (gateway-mode session, not CLI)
OS: Linux
security.redact_secrets: true, security.tirith_enabled: true (both at their documented defaults)
I was not able to diff this against current main (the file has grown to 14k+ lines and moves fast); flagging in case the relevant function has since moved or already been touched by other redaction work.


Root Cause


A command containing a credential-shaped string is scanned by Tirith (tools/tirith_security.py::check_command_security). For a GitHub PAT-shaped string, Tirith correctly returns:


`json   {"action":"block","findings":[{"rule_id":"credential_in_text","severity":"HIGH","title":"GitHub PAT detected","description":"A credential matching a known provider pattern was found in the input. Credentials should not appear in commands or pasted text.","evidence":[{"type":"text","detail":"Matched GitHub PAT pattern"}],"mitre_id":"T1552"}]}`

Note evidence[].detail deliberately omits the matched value — this redaction is working correctly at the Tirith layer.


tools/approval.py::check_all_command_guards() converts a tirith block/warn verdict into an approvable warning (not a hard block) and builds a combined description from the findings — still redacted at this point.
The gateway-side notify callback (gateway/run.py, function _approval_notify_sync, roughly lines 18108–18170 in my checked-out tree) builds the actual platform message. The plain-text fallback path does this:


```
python   cmd_preview = cmd[:200] + "..." if len(cmd) > 200 else cmd
   msg = (
       f"⚠️ **Dangerous command requires approval:**\n"
       f"```\n{cmd_preview}\n```\n"
       f"Reason: {desc}\n\n"
       f"Reply `/approve` to execute, ..."
   )
```

cmd here is approval_data.get("command", "") — the raw, unmodified command string. It is never passed through agent/redact.py's redact_sensitive_text() before being embedded in msg.


The interesting part: redact_sensitive_text is already imported and used elsewhere in this same file (gateway/run.py, around line 8365, and a RedactingFormatter is used for logging around line 19622). It's a one-line fix to apply it here too — the utility already exists, is already enabled by default, and is already proven to work in this exact file. It's just not called in this one function.


Reproduction


Start a Telegram gateway session with approvals.mode: manual (or smart, same path) and security.tirith_enabled: true.
Have the agent run a command that writes a GitHub-PAT-shaped string somewhere, e.g.:


`bash   echo "GITHUB_TOKEN=[REDACTED:github-token]" > /tmp/test.txt`


Observe the Telegram approval prompt: it correctly identifies this as a credential_in_text / GitHub PAT finding (good), but the message body contains the full command — including the literal ghp_... string — verbatim.


I reproduced this with a synthetic, clearly-fake token (testing a local pre-commit hook's own credential-detection regex, ironically), so nothing real was exposed in my case. But the same code path would do the identical thing with a real leaked credential.

Expected vs Actual


Expected: When a Tirith finding's rule_id indicates a credential/secret category, the approval message should not re-expose the matched value — show the (already-redacted) finding description only, or at minimum run the raw command through redact_sensitive_text() before embedding it.
Actual: The raw command, including the credential substring, is sent unmodified to the messaging platform.


Suggested Fix

In _approval_notify_sync (and any sibling implementations for other platforms — Discord/Slack/etc. looked like they share this contract based on issue #41769's note that "Apply the same policy across button platforms"), either:


(a) Pass cmd through agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text() before building cmd_preview / msg, same as the existing usage elsewhere in this file, or
(b) When any finding in approval_data has a credential-related rule_id (Tirith's naming, e.g. credential_in_text), suppress the raw command entirely from the rendered message and show only the finding's description/title fields, which are already safe by construction.


(a) is more general (catches non-Tirith credential shapes too, e.g. password literals that don't trip Tirith's specific rule set); (b) is more conservative and guaranteed not to break legitimate non-credential approval messages. Possibly worth doing both.

Additional Context

This surfaced from issue #16843/#16700-adjacent territory (secret redaction vs. functional command use) but is a distinct gap — those are about redaction breaking real credential usage; this is about redaction not applying at all on the approval-notification path specifically. Also related in spirit to #41769 (approval card metadata not matching backend semantics across platforms) — same family of "approval surface drifted from what the backend layer already knows/enforces."

Happy to provide more detail or test against a patch if useful.

items.title: Telegram polling gateway silently stops receiving messages after TCP CLOSE-WAIT on long-poll socket (ep_poll on dead connection)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

In polling mode, a Hermes Telegram gateway can enter a **silent-but-alive** state where:
- `systemctl --user status hermes-gateway-luna.service` shows `active (running)`
- Memory is stable (~1.5–2 GB after long uptime)
- No log output for 30+ minutes
- The gateway does **not** restart, no error is raised
- All new Telegram messages are silently ignored

## Root cause

The Telegram long-poll loop (`getUpdates`) runs inside httpx / PTB's networking stack over a persistent TCP connection. When the Telegram server silently drops the TCP session (network interruption, NAT timeout, server-side FIN), the OS socket enters **`CLOSE-WAIT`** state.

From the kernel's perspective the socket is still "readable" — `epoll` sees it as ready. `httpx` does not raise an exception because it never attempts a new write on the dead socket. PTB's `Updater` loop, which only reads, never sees an error. The `error_callback` is never triggered. The reconnect ladder is never entered.

Confirmed via `ss -tp | grep <PID>` showing 3 `CLOSE-WAIT` connections to `149.154.166.110:https` (Telegram's IP range), while `cat /proc/<PID>/wchan` shows `ep_poll` — the process is parked waiting on a dead socket.

## Reproduction

Observed on:
- Ubuntu 22.04, Linux 6.8 (Oracle Cloud), Python 3.11.15, PTB 22.6, httpx 0.28.x
- Triggered by network interruptions on the path to `api.telegram.org` (confirmed in logs: `polling reconnect failed: Timed out` × 6, then `Primary api.telegram.org connection failed () → fallback IPs`)
- Timeline: gateway goes silent 30–90 min after a reconnect failure event, persisting indefinitely until manual `systemctl restart`

Diagnostic sequence:
```bash
PID=$(systemctl --user show hermes-gateway-luna.service -p MainPID --value)
ss -tp | grep $PID          # shows CLOSE-WAIT to 149.154.x.x:443
cat /proc/$PID/wchan        # ep_poll
journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway-luna.service --no-pager -n 30
# → last entry is 30+ min old, no errors
```

## Why existing recovery doesn't trigger

| Mechanism | Why it misses this failure |
|---|---|
| `_looks_like_network_error` + `error_callback` | Only fires if PTB raises — which never happens on a CLOSE-WAIT socket (no write attempted, no exception) |
| `_verify_polling_after_reconnect` | One-shot probe, runs only immediately after an explicit reconnect event |
| `Restart=always` (systemd) | Only restarts on process exit — process stays alive spinning on `ep_poll` |
| httpx `keepalive_expiry` | PTB constructs its own `HTTPXRequest` and does not use Hermes's `_http_client_limits.py` helper |

## Relation to #42909

Issue #42909 and PR #42959 describe a related but distinct failure (PTB Updater wedged at the application layer, detected via `pending_update_count`). The CLOSE-WAIT failure described here sits one layer lower: the TCP socket itself is dead, so no `getUpdates` is even attempted. The two watchdog mechanisms are complementary.

## Proposed fix

Add a **persistent heartbeat loop** (`_polling_heartbeat_loop`) that runs as a background `asyncio.Task` for the full lifetime of the polling connection:

1. Sleep for a configurable interval (default: 60 s)
2. Call `await asyncio.wait_for(bot.get_me(), timeout=10)` — a lightweight API call on a **separate** connection from the long-poll socket
3. If `asyncio.TimeoutError` or `OSError` is raised → TCP path to Telegram is broken → call `_handle_polling_network_error()` to enter the existing reconnect ladder
4. All other exceptions (e.g. `TelegramError: Unauthorized`) are swallowed — non-connectivity, should not trigger reconnect
5. On `asyncio.CancelledError` → exit silently (normal shutdown)

The heartbeat starts in `connect()` after `start_polling()` succeeds and is cancelled+awaited in `disconnect()`. This bounds the silent-failure window to `interval + timeout` (≤ 70 s at defaults).

A fix PR will follow referencing this issue.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop remote startup fails when profile listing exceeds hardcoded 15s API timeout
items.body:
# [Bug]: Desktop remote startup fails when profile listing exceeds hardcoded 15s API timeout

## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop remote gateway mode can prove the remote backend is reachable, then still fail startup because subsequent authenticated Desktop API calls use a hardcoded 15 second request timeout.

On a large multi-profile install, the slow call is profile loading. The Desktop log flow is effectively:

```text
Remote Hermes backend is ready
Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
Could not connect to Hermes gateway
```

This is confusing because the backend is not down and auth/reachability are not the root issue. The local Desktop client is timing out while loading startup data from the already-ready remote backend. In the affected setup, profile loading can take roughly 35 seconds, so the macOS Desktop app cannot connect without a source patch or rebuild.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a remote Hermes Dashboard/gateway with many profiles, or otherwise make `GET /api/profiles` take longer than 15 seconds.
2. Configure Hermes Desktop on macOS to use that remote backend.
3. Confirm that the remote backend is reachable and `/api/status` responds quickly.
4. Save/reconnect or launch Desktop.
5. Desktop reports the backend ready, then fails while the renderer/startup code loads authenticated API data such as `/api/profiles`.

## Expected Behavior

Remote Desktop startup should tolerate slower profile-heavy installations after the backend readiness check has passed.

At minimum:

- the startup timeout should be configurable from Desktop settings, or
- remote startup/profile endpoints should use a longer endpoint-specific timeout, or
- profile loading should be lazy/asynchronous so it does not block the entire connection, and
- the error should name the API path that timed out instead of reporting a generic gateway failure.

## Actual Behavior

Desktop shows a generic gateway connection failure even though:

- the remote backend is reachable,
- `/api/status` has already passed, and
- the failure happens in a later authenticated startup API call.

The user-facing result is a dead end: the remote Hermes deployment works, but Desktop cannot be configured to wait long enough for profile loading.

## Affected Component

Other: Desktop remote gateway / Electron API bridge / profile listing.

## Messaging Platform

N/A.

## Debug Report

Not included in this public draft because the available logs contain private deployment details. The relevant sanitized log signature is:

```text
Remote Hermes backend is ready
Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
Could not connect to Hermes gateway
```

## Operating System

- Client: macOS Desktop app
- Backend: remote Linux Hermes Dashboard/gateway

## Hermes Version

Observed against current Desktop behavior on the `main`-line source checked locally at commit `2f7c4858a764ca32c66e0ef5d90b2d8b8f1792da`.

## Root Cause Analysis

The Desktop readiness check and the later authenticated API calls use different effective timing behavior.

Source references from the checked `main` clone:

- `apps/desktop/electron/hardening.cjs:6` sets `DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs:2634` applies that timeout in `fetchJson(...)`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs:2690-2692` destroys the request with `Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after ${timeoutMs}ms`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs:3277-3291` gives `waitForHermes(...)` a 45 second readiness window, but that readiness loop only probes `/api/status`.
- `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts:588-591` exposes `getProfiles()` as `path: '/api/profiles'`.
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py:9164-9168` implements `GET /api/profiles` as an `async def` that directly calls `profiles_mod.list_profiles()`.
- `hermes_cli/profiles.py:716-780` shows `list_profiles()` scanning each profile and reading per-profile metadata/config/state.

That means Desktop can pass the readiness probe, then immediately fail on a slower profile-heavy endpoint because the authenticated REST helper still defaults to 15 seconds.

This also overlaps with a broader pattern in existing issues where Desktop reports backend readiness but later API calls time out:

- #43429: Desktop backend reports ready but Electron API requests time out.
- #45072: dashboard backend can block/starve HTTP/WS during Desktop boot.
- #44560: another 15 second Desktop API timeout path around model options.
- #48434: remote Desktop reconnect failures after successful auth.

This issue is specifically the remote Desktop + large profile-listing facet.

## Proposed Fix

Short-term Desktop-side fix:

- Add a configurable remote backend request timeout in Desktop settings, for example `Remote backend request timeout`.
- Use a safer default for remote authenticated startup calls, e.g. 60 seconds, while preserving a shorter default for purely local/lightweight probes if desired.
- Include the timed-out API path and timeout duration in the thrown error.

Server/profile endpoint fix:

- Avoid doing full profile scanning on the FastAPI event loop for `GET /api/profiles`.
- Consider moving `profiles_mod.list_profiles()` into a worker thread, caching profile summaries briefly, or returning a lightweight profile index first and loading expensive per-profile metadata lazily.

The best user experience would combine both: Desktop should not hard-fail remote startup at 15 seconds, and the profile endpoint should avoid blocking remote boot on full per-profile scans.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Potentially, yes.

items.title: [BUG] Sub-profile gateway: sessions.json populated but state.db remains empty — complete session data loss (related to #40344, #46144)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
# [BUG] Sub-profile gateway: sessions created in sessions.json but state.db remains empty — complete session data loss

## Summary

When running Hermes gateway under a **sub-profile** (non-default profile via `HERMES_HOME` env var), conversations are processed correctly (sessions.json records them, responses are delivered), but **zero data is persisted to state.db**. The state.db file is initialized with schema (SCHEMA_VERSION=15) but contains 0 sessions and 0 messages. WAL files are 0 bytes.

This affects ALL sub-profile gateways in a multi-profile deployment. In our case, 4 sub-profiles (dev-pony, marketing-pony, kehu-tuozhan-xiaoqi, laiven-assistant) each running independent gateway processes with `HERMES_HOME` set correctly — 3 out of 4 have completely empty state.db despite sessions.json showing 7/4/2 active sessions respectively.

**Related issues**: #40344 (WebUI profile state.db not created), #46144 (TUI writes to wrong profile's state.db). This is the **gateway variant** of the same profile→state.db routing bug class.

## Environment

- **OS**: WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows
- **Hermes version**: Latest main (as of 2026-06-18, commit range covering May-June 2026)
- **Deployment**: 5 concurrent gateway processes (1 default + 4 sub-profiles), each started via:
  ```bash
  setsid bash -c 'HERMES_HOME=/path/to/profile hermes gateway run --replace > /tmp/gateway-PORT.log 2>&1'
  ```
- **Platform**: WeCom (Enterprise WeChat)

## Evidence

### 1. sessions.json has data, state.db is empty

```
dev-pony/sessions.json:       7 session keys, latest updated 2026-06-13
dev-pony/state.db:            0 sessions, 0 messages, WAL=0 bytes

marketing-pony/sessions.json: 4 session keys, latest updated 2026-06-14
marketing-pony/state.db:      0 sessions, 0 messages, WAL=0 bytes

kehu-tuozhan-xiaoqi/sessions.json: 2 session keys
kehu-tuozhan-xiaoqi/state.db:      0 sessions, 0 messages, WAL=0 bytes

laiven-assistant/sessions.json: 1 session key
laiven-assistant/state.db:      1 session, 3 messages ← ONLY working profile
```

### 2. File descriptors confirm correct state.db is open

```
PID 244040 (dev-pony):         fd/11 → profiles/dev-pony/state.db ✓
PID 244077 (marketing-pony):   fd/11 → profiles/marketing-pony/state.db-wal
PID 244093 (kehu-tuozhan-xiaoqi): fd/10 → profiles/kehu-tuozhan-xiaoqi/state.db
```

### 3. HERMES_HOME resolves correctly at import time

```python
>>> HERMES_HOME=.../profiles/dev-pony python3 -c "from hermes_state import DEFAULT_DB_PATH; print(DEFAULT_DB_PATH)"
.../profiles/dev-pony/state.db  # CORRECT
```

### 4. No SQLite errors in gateway logs

All gateway logs are clean — no "Session DB operation failed" warnings.

### 5. auto_prune ran recently

```
dev-pony: last_auto_prune 4.5h ago, ghost_session_prune_v1=1
marketing-pony: last_auto_prune 4.5h ago
```

### 6. Sessions did NOT leak to main state.db

Main state.db has only 2 wecom sessions (from default profile's own gateway). Sub-profile sessions are completely lost — not written anywhere.

## Suspected Root Causes (3 candidates)

### Candidate A: Silent create_session() failure → FK cascade

In `gateway/session.py:966-970`:
```python
if self._db and db_create_kwargs:
    try:
        self._db.create_session(**db_create_kwargs)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[gateway] Warning: Failed to create SQLite session: {e}")
```

If `create_session()` fails (e.g., transient SQLite lock), the session row is never created. Subsequently, `append_message()` with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` fails because `session_id` references a non-existent row. Both failures are caught silently.

### Candidate B: DEFAULT_DB_PATH module-level evaluation timing

`hermes_state.py:34`:
```python
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = get_hermes_home() / "state.db"
```

This is evaluated at **import time**. If `hermes_state` is imported before `HERMES_HOME` is set (e.g., by a parent process or shared import cache), `DEFAULT_DB_PATH` resolves to `~/.hermes/state.db` — the default profile. All `SessionDB()` calls then write to the wrong file.

However, our fd evidence shows the correct file IS open, suggesting this is not the primary cause in our deployment.

### Candidate C: auto_prune / ghost_session_prune deleted valid sessions

`state_meta` shows `ghost_session_prune_v1=1` on dev-pony. If the ghost-session heuristic incorrectly identifies sub-profile sessions as ghosts (e.g., sessions created in DB but with `message_count=0` because `append_message` failed), it would delete them.

This is the most dangerous scenario: data is written, then silently removed by maintenance.

## Impact

1. **session_search completely broken** for sub-profiles — `session_search()` tool returns empty results
2. **/resume, /title, /history, /branch all fail** for sub-profile sessions
3. **Conversation history lost** — agent cannot recall previous interactions
4. **Cron job context injection fails** — `context_from` references produce no data
5. **Desktop/TUI sidebar shows no sessions** for sub-profiles
6. **Multi-agent team coordination impaired** — cross-profile session queries return nothing

## Reproduction

1. Create a sub-profile: `hermes profile create test-sub`
2. Start gateway with HERMES_HOME: `HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes/profiles/test-sub hermes gateway run`
3. Send messages via any connected platform
4. Check: `sqlite3 ~/.hermes/profiles/test-sub/state.db "SELECT count(*) FROM sessions"` → **0**
5. Check: `cat ~/.hermes/profiles/test-sub/sessions/sessions.json` → **has entries**

## Willing to Submit PR

Yes. I can provide:
- A diagnostic script that detects the condition
- A fix for the silent failure path (elevate logging, add retry)
- A fix for ghost_session_prune to not delete sessions that have sessions.json entries

## Additional Context

This is a **data-loss bug** — not a cosmetic issue. In our production deployment, 3 out of 4 sub-profile agents have been operating without any persistent session history for 10+ days. Every conversation is effectively amnesia-on-restart.

items.title: `hermes update` 后 agent-browser 全局软链变成死链，导致 browser 工具失效（dangling symlink to internal path）

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## 问题描述

执行 `hermes update` 之后，`/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser` 这个全局软链接会变成**指向 hermes-agent 内部不存在的目录的死链**，导致：

- `which agent-browser` 仍然能找到命令（软链存在，PATH 里有）
- 但实际执行 `agent-browser --version` 报 `command not found`（exit 127）
- Hermes 内置的 `browser_navigate` / `browser_snapshot` / `browser_click` / `browser_screenshot` / `browser_console` / `browser_type` / `browser_press` / `browser_scroll` / `browser_back` / `browser_get_images` / `browser_vision` 等所有 browser 工具全部失效

## 复现（已发生 ≥2 次）

- **2026-06-12 13:45**：报告 session `20260612_134521_b35e6a`
- **2026-06-19 00:19**：报告 session（本次），hermes update 后复发

**两次都满足的条件**：

1. 用户已经通过 `npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.1` 全局安装
2. 用户执行 `hermes update`（或者任何触发 `tools_config.py` 中 `post_setup_key in {"agent_browser", "browserbase"}` 分支的命令，例如 `hermes acp --setup-browser`）
3. 之后 `/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser` 软链目标变成 `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64`，**但该内部路径已不存在**

**实际复现命令序列**：

```bash
# 1. 正常态
$ agent-browser --version
agent-browser 0.27.1

$ ls -la /opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser
lrwxr-xr-x ... /opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser -> /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64

# 2. 执行 hermes update
$ hermes update
... (update 过程中 tools_config.py 跑了 post_setup)

# 3. 软链被改回，指向 hermes-agent 内部
$ ls -la /opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser
lrwxr-xr-x ... /opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser -> /Users/linyunjian/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64

$ ls -la /Users/linyunjian/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64
ls: ... No such file or directory

# 4. 实际跑就炸
$ agent-browser --version
/bin/bash: line 1: agent-browser: command not found
# exit 127
```

## 根本原因

**链路 1：post-setup 强制安装 → 软链被改向 → 目标丢失**

1. `hermes-agent/package.json` 第 36 行声明依赖 `"agent-browser": "^0.26.0"`
2. `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/tools_config.py` 第 836 行附近的 post-setup 钩子**强制**调用 `npm install` 把 agent-browser 装到 hermes-agent 自己的 `node_modules/agent-browser/`（参见代码 `node_modules = PROJECT_ROOT / "node_modules" / "agent-browser"`）
3. 每次 `hermes update` 触发该钩子时，**npm install 会重新生成/清理内部 node_modules 目录**——这会**直接破坏**用户已有的全局软链 `/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser`
4. 软链的旧目标（npm 全局 `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/...`）**没被破坏**，但 `tools_config.py` 的 npm install 行为**改了软链的目标**，改成 hermes-agent 内部路径
5. 而 hermes-agent 自身的 `node_modules/agent-browser/` 在 update 后**也可能**因为源码与 npm 包结构差异而**没真正落地**那个二进制（参见 6 月 11 日诊断：源是 `.git` 仓库而非 npm 包），结果就是**软链目标整个不存在**
6. 现在：软链在、目标丢、`which` 找得到、跑不动、`agent-browser: command not found`

**链路 2：`browser_tool.py` 没做 dangling symlink 校验**

`hermes-agent/tools/browser_tool.py` 第 1782-1809 行的查找顺序：

```python
# 1. PATH 里找
which_result = shutil.which("agent-browser")
if which_result:
    _cached_agent_browser = which_result  # ← 拿到就缓存，不验证

# 2. 扩展 PATH 找
extended_path = _merge_browser_path("")
...
which_result = shutil.which("agent-browser", path=extended_path)
if which_result:
    _cached_agent_browser = which_result

# 3. 本地 node_modules/.bin/ 找
local_bin_dir = repo_root / "node_modules" / ".bin"
local_which = shutil.which("agent-browser", path=str(local_bin_dir))
```

**问题**：`shutil.which` 找到的只是"PATH 里存在的可执行名字"，**不验证它是不是 dangling symlink**，更不验证它**真的能跑**。所以：
- `which agent-browser` 返回 `/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser`（软链在）
- 软链目标不存在 → `subprocess.run(['agent-browser', ...])` 时 OS 报 `No such file or directory`
- `_cached_agent_browser` 还**缓存**了这个无效路径，下次再调还是炸

**链路 3：`dep_ensure.py` / `doctor.py` / `nous_subscription.py` 的依赖检测同样不可靠**

- `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/dep_ensure.py:28-32` 行的 `browser` 检查用 `shutil.which("agent-browser") is not None`——**不验证可执行**
- `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/doctor.py:1431-1440` 行的 `agent-browser (Node.js)` 同样只看 `agent_browser_path.exists()`——**不验证能不能跑**
- `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/nous_subscription.py:153-159` 行用 `shutil.which("agent-browser") or local_bin.exists()`——**同上**

三处都用"`which` 能找到"当作"能用"的依据，**忽略了 dangling symlink** 的情况。

## 期望行为

当用户系统已经有可用的 `agent-browser` 时：

1. **不要**强制重新安装到 hermes-agent 自己的 `node_modules/agent-browser/`
2. **直接复用 PATH 里的版本**
3. 如果软链被破坏或目标不存在，**给出明确报错**（"agent-browser 命令存在但无法执行，请运行 `npm install -g agent-browser` 修复"），而不是**悄悄静默失败**
4. 所有依赖检测和工具调用都应做 **dangling symlink 校验**（`os.access(path, os.X_OK)` + `--version` 的轻量 sanity check），确认命令真的能跑

## 实际行为

post-setup 钩子无脑 `npm install`：

1. 把软链目标改成 hermes-agent 内部路径
2. 但 hermes-agent 内部路径在 update 后**可能根本不存在**（因为源是 git 仓库，不是 npm 包安装结果）
3. `browser_tool.py` 用 `shutil.which` 缓存了无效路径
4. `subprocess.run(['agent-browser', ...])` 报 `No such file or directory`
5. `doctor` / `dep_ensure` / `nous_subscription` 都说 agent-browser 可用——**全是假阳性**
6. **整个 browser 工具链失效**，用户必须手动 `ln -sf` 重指软链或 `npm install -g agent-browser` 修复

## 建议修复

### 修复 1：`tools_config.py` post-setup 改为"PATH 优先，不重复安装"

修改 `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/tools_config.py` 第 836-920 行的 post-setup 逻辑：

```python
if post_setup_key in {"agent_browser", "browserbase"}:
    # 先检查 PATH 里是否已经有可用的 agent-browser
    import shutil, subprocess
    existing = shutil.which("agent-browser")
    if existing and os.path.exists(existing) and os.access(existing, os.X_OK):
        # 实际跑一次 --version 做 sanity check
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                [existing, "--version"],
                capture_output=True,
                timeout=5,
                check=True
            )
            # 完全可用，跳过安装
            return {"status": "ok", "path": existing, "action": "skip-install"}
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError):
            # 软链死了或执行失败，走修复流程
            pass

    # PATH 里没有或者坏了，再走原本的 npm install 流程
    node_modules = PROJECT_ROOT / "node_modules" / "agent-browser"
    ...
```

### 修复 2：`browser_tool.py` 查找后做 dangling symlink 校验

`hermes-agent/tools/browser_tool.py` 第 1782-1809 行，找到 `shutil.which` 结果后必须做：

```python
def _is_usable_agent_browser(path: str) -> bool:
    """检查路径是否是真能跑的 agent-browser 二进制"""
    import os, subprocess
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path) or not os.access(path, os.X_OK):
        return False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [path, "--version"],
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=5
        )
        return result.returncode == 0
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError):
        return False
```

在缓存到 `_cached_agent_browser` 之前用 `_is_usable_agent_browser(which_result)` 校验，**不通过就跳过该候选**继续找下一个（PATH → 扩展 PATH → 本地 node_modules/.bin）。

### 修复 3：`dep_ensure.py` / `doctor.py` / `nous_subscription.py` 同步加可执行校验

三处文件都把 `shutil.which("agent-browser")` 这种"看名字在不在"的检查**升级**为"看名字 + 实际跑 `--version` 验证"。建议抽成共享 helper（避免三处重复实现）。

### 修复 4（可选）：让 `package.json` 的 agent-browser 依赖变成可选

把 `hermes-agent/package.json` 第 36 行的 `"agent-browser": "^0.26.0"` 从 `dependencies` 移到 `optionalDependencies` 或 `peerDependenciesMeta`，并明确"如果用户已通过全局安装提供，hermes-agent 不应再装自己的版本"。

## 环境信息

- **OS**：macOS 26.x（darwin arm64）
- **Node.js**：`>= 20.0.0`（来自 `hermes-agent/package.json` engines 字段）
- **实际安装版本**：
  - 全局 npm 装的：`agent-browser@0.27.1`（装在 `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/agent-browser/`）
  - hermes-agent 内部声明的：`^0.26.0`（来自 `hermes-agent/package.json` 第 36 行 + `package-lock.json` 第 8946 行钉死 `0.26.0`）
- **受影响代码**：
  - `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/tools_config.py:836` — post-setup 强制安装逻辑
  - `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/dep_ensure.py:28-32` — 依赖检测
  - `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/doctor.py:1431-1440` — doctor 健康检查
  - `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/nous_subscription.py:153-159` — 订阅检查
  - `hermes-agent/tools/browser_tool.py:1782-1809` — 实际调用入口
- **未受影响（已确认）**：
  - `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/agent-browser/` 目录本身没被破坏
  - `npm root -g` 路径（`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`）没变
  - 用户手工 `ln -sf` 修复后立即可用：`agent-browser 0.27.1`

## 备注

我（报告人）已经查过 `package.json`、`package-lock.json`、`tools/browser_tool.py`、`hermes_cli/tools_config.py`、`hermes_cli/dep_ensure.py`、`hermes_cli/doctor.py`、`hermes_cli/nous_subscription.py` 的源码，确认问题链路如上。

问题本质是 **Hermes 在 update 时无脑重新安装内部 agent-browser，但实际可能没装到位**（源是 git 仓库而非 npm 包），同时**全链路缺乏 dangling symlink 校验**——`shutil.which` 找到的无效路径一路被缓存到 `_cached_agent_browser`，导致 `subprocess.run` 静默失败。

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Bug Report: SessionDB API signature mismatch causes runtime errors

## Summary

Two `SessionDB` methods in `hermes_state.py` reject keyword arguments passed by callers, causing repeated `TypeError` warnings in the agent logs. The errors degrade session persistence — messages are silently dropped and session creation fails until retry.

## Affected methods

| File | Line | Method | Unexpected kwarg | Caller(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hermes_state.py` | 745 | `_insert_session_row()` | `cwd` | `acp_adapter/server.py:1115,1186` via `session_manager.create_session(cwd=cwd)` → `create_session(**kwargs)` |
| `hermes_state.py` | 1621 | `append_message()` | `timestamp` | `run_agent.py:1655`, `gateway/session.py:1326` |

## Error messages

```
SessionDB._insert_session_row() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cwd'
SessionDB.append_message() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timestamp'
```



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Using the :latest tag `docker compose pull && docker compose down && docker compose up -d`

### Expected Behavior

No database schema issues with the latest docker image.

### Actual Behavior

Database scheme issues.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
n/a
```

### Operating System

Docker image

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

0.16.0 and :latest docker image

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root cause

`create_session()` forwards `**kwargs` directly to `_insert_session_row()`, but `_insert_session_row()` has a closed signature — it does not accept `**kwargs`. When `acp_adapter/server.py` calls `session_manager.create_session(cwd=cwd)`, the `cwd` kwarg flows through and blows up.

Similarly, `run_agent.py` and `gateway/session.py` pass `timestamp=message.get("timestamp")` to `append_message()`, which also has a closed signature that doesn't include `timestamp`.

The callers were updated to pass these new fields, but the `SessionDB` method signatures were never updated to accept them.

## Impact

- **Session creation fails** for ACP adapter sessions — retries succeed only if the caller drops `cwd` on retry (which it doesn't, so it keeps failing).
- **Messages silently dropped** — `run_agent.py:1660` catches the exception and logs a warning, but the message is never persisted to `state.db`.
- **Session search (`session_search`) returns incomplete data** since messages are missing.



### Proposed Fix (optional)

## Recommended fix

Add `**kwargs` to both method signatures to absorb caller kwargs that the methods don't need to process:

labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

The built-in Anthropic OAuth flow (`hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` / `hermes model` → Anthropic → Claude Max OAuth) fails at token exchange with:

```
Token exchange failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
Anthropic OAuth login did not return credentials.
```

The authorize step and the user's subscription are fine — the failure is the token-exchange POST.

## Root cause

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py` POSTs to `https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token` with a spoofed `User-Agent: claude-cli/<version> (external, cli)`. Anthropic now **404s that token endpoint for any `claude-cli/` User-Agent prefix**.

Reproduced (Jun 18 2026) — same JSON body, varying only the UA:

| User-Agent | Result |
|---|---|
| `claude-cli/2.1.74 (external, cli)` | **404** |
| `claude-cli/2.1.143` | **404** |
| `claude-cli/2.1.179` | **404** |
| `curl/8` | 429 (endpoint reachable) |
| empty | 403 |
| `foo/1.0` | 400 |

So `_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_FALLBACK` bumps **do not** fix it — every `claude-cli/*` UA is blocked regardless of version. The code comment around `anthropic_adapter.py:342` ("Anthropic rejects OAuth requests when the spoofed user-agent version is too far behind") anticipated a *version* gate, but the actual change is a *UA-prefix* block.

## Repro

```python
import urllib.request, json
data = json.dumps({
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "client_id": "9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e",
    "code": "x", "state": "y",
    "redirect_uri": "https://console.anthropic.com/oauth/code/callback",
    "code_verifier": "z",
}).encode()
req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token",
    data=data,
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
             "User-Agent": "claude-cli/2.1.179 (external, cli)"},
    method="POST",
)
urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15)  # -> HTTP Error 404
```

Swap the UA to `curl/8` and the same request reaches the endpoint (429), confirming the endpoint exists and the discriminator is the `claude-cli/` UA prefix, not the request body or version.

## Working alternative (what unblocked me)

The genuine `claude setup-token` flow (from `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`) uses a **different endpoint** — `claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize` → `platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback` — which Anthropic accepts. It mints a 1-year `sk-ant-oat…` token that Hermes already consumes via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

Suggested fix: migrate the built-in flow to the `claude.com/cai/oauth` + `platform.claude.com` endpoints (and/or stop spoofing the `claude-cli` UA), rather than maintaining a version constant that can no longer help.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), upstream `5ffbfed1`
- Linux, Python 3.11

items.title: [Bug]: Dashboard "paste image" reads the SERVER's clipboard, not the browser's — image paste impossible on any remote/Docker deployment
items.body:
## Component
Dashboard / tui_gateway (web UI), clipboard image attachment

## Hermes version
v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)

## Environment
- Hermes runs **headless inside a Docker container** (deployed via 1Panel), `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119`
- User accesses the dashboard from a **Windows desktop via a web browser** (remote machine, different OS)
- Container has no GUI: no `DISPLAY`, no Wayland, no `xclip`/`xsel`/`wl-paste`, not WSL

## Summary
On the web Dashboard, pasting an image into the chat never works for any deployment where the browser and the Hermes process are on **different machines** (Docker, remote server, VPS, etc.). The paste path resolves the clipboard on the **server side**, so it inspects the container's clipboard instead of the user's browser clipboard.

## Root cause (traced in source)
The dashboard chat is the embedded xterm TUI (`ui-tui/dist/entry.js`). Its paste handler `paste2` calls:

```js
rpc("clipboard.paste", { session_id: getUiState().sid })
```

The frontend never captures the browser clipboard image (no `clipboardData`/`getAsFile`/`FileReader`/`readAsDataURL` in the paste path). It delegates entirely to the backend.

The backend handler `@method("clipboard.paste")` in `tui_gateway/server.py` calls:

```python
from hermes_cli.clipboard import has_clipboard_image, save_clipboard_image
...
if not save_clipboard_image(img_path):   # reads the SERVER process's clipboard
```

`hermes_cli/clipboard.py::save_clipboard_image()` branches on `sys.platform` of the **Hermes process** and shells out to OS clipboard tools (`pbpaste`/PowerShell/`xclip`/`wl-paste`) on the **machine Hermes runs on**. In a headless Linux container this always returns False → user sees **"No image found in clipboard"**, even though the image is sitting in the Windows browser clipboard.

This is an architectural assumption that the browser and the Hermes process share the same clipboard — only true for a purely local dashboard. For the documented remote/Docker dashboard deployment it cannot work.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119` inside a headless Linux Docker container.
2. From a different machine (e.g. Windows), open the dashboard in a browser.
3. Copy an image to the OS clipboard, focus the chat, paste (Ctrl+V) or run the paste action.
4. Result: "No image found in clipboard". The image is never attached.

## Expected behavior
When the dashboard is accessed remotely, pasting/dropping an image in the browser should upload the image **bytes from the browser** to the backend, which then saves it under `$HERMES_HOME/images/` and attaches it via the existing `image.attach` / `attached_images` flow.

## Suggested fix
Add a browser-side → server upload path instead of server-side clipboard reads:
- Frontend: on `paste`/`drop`, read `clipboardData.items` / `DataTransferItem.getAsFile()`, base64-encode, and send to a new RPC (e.g. `image.upload` with `{ data_b64, filename, mime }`) or a multipart HTTP endpoint.
- Backend: decode/persist to `$HERMES_HOME/images/`, then reuse the existing `attached_images` append logic (same as `image.attach`).
- Keep the current `clipboard.paste` (server-side) only for the genuinely-local dashboard case, and/or feature-detect remote sessions to hide/disable the misleading server-side paste.

## Current workarounds (for other remote users hitting this)
- Reference an image already on the server: `/image /path/in/container/img.png` (works because `image.attach` takes a server path).
- Send the image via a connected messaging platform (Feishu/Telegram/etc.) — those download the media via platform APIs and bypass the clipboard entirely.
- Paste an image URL and let the agent fetch it.

items.title: [Bug]: Matrix DM rooms with auto-set names incorrectly classified as room, require @mention

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

After Hermes v0.16.0, Matrix DM rooms that have been assigned a room name (by the client) are incorrectly classified as chat_type="room" instead of "dm". This causes the require_mention gating to apply, forcing the user to @mention the bot even in a legitimate one-on-one DM.

**Root cause:** In _resolve_room_identity() at gateway/platforms/matrix.py:3677:

chat_type = "dm" if is_direct and not has_explicit_name else "room"

The heuristic treats any room with an explicit name as a non-DM, on the assumption that named rooms are probably stale m.direct entries for rooms that later became groups. However, most Matrix clients automatically set a room name when creating a DM (e.g., "Alice & Bot" from participant display names). This means virtually all client-created DM rooms fail the not has_explicit_name check.

**Difference from #44679 / #44700:** PR #44700 fixes the case where the bot has no m.direct data at all (fresh account). But even with that fix merged, is_direct becomes True for a DM room and yet the has_explicit_name check on line 3677 still overrides it, so the room remains classified as room. The two bugs are distinct.

### Severity

High. Affects any Matrix user whose client auto-names DM rooms (Element, SchildiChat, FluffyChat, and most other Matrix clients do this by default). Users in DM rooms must @mention the bot on every message.

### Proposed Fix

Use member_count (already fetched on line 3673 as await self._get_room_member_count(room_id)) as a secondary signal. A room with member_count <= 2 that is also in m.direct is almost certainly a DM, regardless of whether it has an explicit name.

is_likely_dm = is_direct and (not has_explicit_name or (member_count is not None and member_count <= 2))
chat_type = "dm" if is_likely_dm else "room"

This handles:
- Unnamed DM: remains classified as DM (existing logic)
- Named DM (<=2 members): classified as DM (new behavior, fixes this bug)
- Room that gained 3+ members: classified as room (stale m.direct handled correctly)
- Pure group chat (not in m.direct): classified as room (unchanged)
- member_count is None: falls back to existing has_explicit_name logic (safe)

### Environment
- Hermes version: v0.16.0+
- Matrix adapter: gateway/platforms/matrix.py

items.title: [Bug]: in-process file tools resolve ~ (tilde) using gateway HOME, not profile HOME, breaking cron jobs with tilde paths

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

In-process file tools resolve `~` (tilde) using `os.path.expanduser()`, which reads the process's `HOME` environment variable. When Hermes runs under a gateway (Docker, systemd, s6, etc.), the gateway process's `HOME` often differs from the interactive CLI session's `HOME` — especially in profile mode where the session wrapper sets `HOME={HERMES_HOME}/home`. Cron jobs running inside the gateway inherit the gateway's `HOME`, so `~` expands to the wrong directory and file operations fail.

The `home_mode` setting (`auto | real | profile`) only affects the terminal tool's subprocesses via `get_subprocess_home()`. In-process tools (`write_file`, `read_file`, `patch`, `search_files`) bypass this entirely and use raw `os.path.expanduser()`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes in a container or service manager where the gateway process has a different `HOME` than the interactive session (e.g., Docker with gateway `HOME=/opt/data`, profile session `HOME=/opt/data/profiles/coder/home`)
2. Create a cron job with a prompt containing `~/some/path/` (or any tilde path)
3. The cron job runs inside the gateway process and `~` expands using the gateway's `HOME`
4. File operations target the wrong directory, failing with `No such file or directory`

### Expected Behavior

`~` should resolve consistently regardless of whether the agent runs in an interactive CLI session or inside a gateway-driven cron job. In-process file tools should use the same HOME resolution as the terminal tool (`get_subprocess_home()`), or the gateway should normalize `HOME` at startup.

### Actual Behavior

The file tool resolves `~` using the gateway's `HOME` instead of the profile's HOME. A cron job prompt referencing `~/profiles/coder/scratch/saber-docs/` expands to a non-existent path under the gateway's HOME, and `write_file` fails with:

```
Failed to write file: .../profiles/coder/scratch/saber-docs/.hermes-tmp.XXXX: No such file or directory
```

The file-mutation verifier correctly reports the file was not modified, but the root cause (HOME mismatch between gateway and session) is opaque to the user.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```
version:          0.16.0 (2026.6.5) [9688c1a9]
os:               Linux 7.0.0-22-generic x86_64
python:           3.13.5
profile:          coder
hermes_home:      /opt/data/profiles/coder
model:            Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-Coding
provider:         custom:lemonade
terminal:         local
gateway:          running (s6 (container supervisor))
platforms:        telegram, discord
cron_jobs:        2 active / 2 total
```

### Operating System

Linux 7.0.0-22-generic x86_64 (Docker container)

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

0.16.0 (2026.6.5)

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

In-process file tools call `os.path.expanduser()` which reads `HOME` directly from the environment. The gateway process has `HOME` set to the system user home (e.g., `/opt/data`), while the interactive session sets `HOME` to the profile-specific directory (e.g., `/opt/data/profiles/coder/home`) via the profile wrapper script.

`hermes_constants.py` provides `get_subprocess_home()` (line 285-308) which returns `{HERMES_HOME}/home` for profile isolation, but this is only used by the terminal tool for subprocess environments. The file tools bypass this entirely.

`cron/scheduler.py` runs cron jobs in-process via `AIAgent()` (line 1726), inheriting the gateway's environment. No HOME override is applied.

Related: `get_hermes_home()` in `hermes_constants.py` (line 53-108) has a comment noting this exact problem:
> "Subprocess spawners are expected to propagate HERMES_HOME explicitly (see the systemd template in hermes_cli/gateway.py and the kanban dispatcher in hermes_cli/kanban_db.py). See https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/18594."

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Option A (preferred): Make file tools use `get_hermes_home()`-aware path expansion. Replace `os.path.expanduser()` with a helper that resolves `~` using `get_subprocess_home()` when available, falling back to `HOME` otherwise.

Option B: Have the gateway set `HOME` to `get_subprocess_home()` at startup (in `gateway/run.py`), so all in-process tools see the correct HOME.

Option C (minimum): Document in the cron docs that `~` is unreliable in cron job prompts and absolute paths should be used. Add a warning when cron prompts contain `~/` paths.

Related issues: #4426 (profiles do not isolate HOME), #18594 (get_hermes_home() falls back to default in profile mode), #4707 (cron falls back to default HERMES_HOME).

items.title: Desktop dashboard zombie processes accumulate on ports 9120-9199

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Environment

- **Hermes Version**: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream 426f321e
- **OS**: macOS 15.7.5 (ARM64)
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **Install Method**: Desktop app (Electron)

## Description

Hermes Desktop spawns `hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9XXX` as child processes for the Python web backend. When the Desktop app exits abnormally (crash, force-quit, update-restart, or macOS killing the process), these child processes are **reparented to launchd (PID 1)** and continue listening on their assigned ports indefinitely.

Over extended usage, this accumulates 50-80+ zombie `python3.11` processes, each holding a TCP LISTEN socket on ports 9120-9199.

## Reproduction

1. Use Hermes Desktop normally over several sessions/days
2. Periodically switch profiles or let the app restart (updates, crashes)
3. Check with: `lsof -i :9120-9199 | grep LISTEN`
4. Observe growing number of orphaned `python3.11` processes

## Evidence

```
$ lsof -i :9120-9199 | grep LISTEN | wc -l
78

$ ps -o pid,ppid,command -p <zombie PID>
PID  PPID COMMAND
858  1    /Users/.../python -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9194
```

## Root Cause

1. **Spawn path**: `cmd_dashboard()` in `hermes_cli/main.py` starts a long-lived uvicorn server as a subprocess
2. **No cleanup on exit**: The Electron main process does not register `will-quit` / `beforeunload` handlers to SIGTERM its Python children
3. **No self-termination**: The Python dashboard has no `atexit` handler, no orphan detection (checking if PPID changed to 1), and no signal handler
4. **Cleanup only on update**: `_kill_stale_dashboard_processes()` only runs on `hermes update` or `hermes dashboard --stop`

Key code locations:
- `_find_stale_dashboard_pids()` — `hermes_cli/main.py:5390`
- `_kill_stale_dashboard_processes()` — `hermes_cli/main.py:5624`
- `cmd_dashboard()` — `hermes_cli/main.py:10312`

## Suggested Fix

**Option A — Electron side** (preferred): Register `app.on('will-quit')` to SIGTERM all spawned Python children.

**Option B — Python side**: Add orphan detection:
```python
def _watch_parent():
    original_ppid = os.getppid()
    while True:
        time.sleep(10)
        if os.getppid() != original_ppid:
            os._exit(0)
threading.Thread(target=_watch_parent, daemon=True).start()
```

**Option C — Both** (belt and suspenders).

## Impact

- ~3 GB wasted RAM (80 zombies × ~40MB RSS)
- Ports 9120-9199 eventually exhausted
- User confusion from dozens of mysterious python processes

## Workaround

```bash
hermes dashboard --stop
# or
lsof -i :9120-9199 -t | xargs kill 2>/dev/null
```

items.title: [Feature]: Add a `langfuse` optional-dependency extra so the bundled `observability/langfuse` plugin is installable on NixOS (uv2nix) + container mode

labels.name: area/nix
labels.description: Nix flake, NixOS module, container packaging

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case


On a `NixOS + Container` Hermes installation, the bundled `plugins/observability/langfuse` plugin is shipped and enableable, but its dependency can't be declared through the supported packaging mechanisms. That makes it impossible to deploy the plugin on a Nix/uv2nix deployment, except by adding a source patch.

The plugin imports the SDK in-process inside the gateway:

```python
from langfuse import Langfuse, propagate_attributes
```

On a `NixOS + Container` install, the gateway runs `current-package/bin/hermes` from the sealed uv2nix venv, which is built strictly from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`. So the SDK has to be in that venv. The supported mechanism for that is `extraDependencyGroups`, but it can only pull an extra that already exists in `pyproject.toml`. But there is no `langfuse` (or `observability`) extra. The other mechanisms don't work either:

- `extraPythonPackages` injects onto PYTHONPATH and runs a name-based collision  check; langfuse shares httpx/pydantic/packaging/wrapt/opentelemetry-\* with the venv, so it exits(1) immediately.
- baking it into a container image doesn't help: the gateway runs from the Nix venv, not the image's system Python.

Because of that, on a `NixOS + Container` Hermes install, the only way to deploy a plugin that is already bundled is through a source patch that adds the missing extra and re-instantiate the package, and regenerate the patch on every release.

(See a working example of that below. That's what I'm doing currently in my install to enable the plugin.)


### Proposed Solution

Add one line to `[project.optional-dependencies]` in `pyproject.toml`, alongside the other existing extras, and regenerate the lock:

```
langfuse = ["langfuse==4.9.0"]
```

Keep it out of `[all]` and `LAZY_DEPS` so default installs are unaffected; it then becomes pullable by name, which is all a packaged plugin needs.

That makes the plugin installable through the normal `extraDependencyGroups` mechanism. On NixOS the entire config then becomes:

```nix
    services.hermes-agent = {
      enable = true;
      extraDependencyGroups = [ "langfuse" ];
      settings.plugins.enabled = [ "observability/langfuse" ];
      environmentFiles = [ "/run/secrets/hermes-langfuse.env" ];  # HERMES_LANGFUSE_* keys
    };
```

Resolution is purely additive and low-risk: at a recent rev, `uv lock` with that line added only `langfuse 4.9.0` and `backoff 2.2.1`; no existing pin (httpx, pydantic, packaging, wrapt, opentelemetry-\*) moved. Both symbols imported by the plugin (`Langfuse`, `propagate_attributes`) are present in 4.x.


### Alternatives Considered

- `extraPythonPackages` onto PYTHONPATH: blocked by the name-based collision check (shared httpx/pydantic/opentelemetry-\* deps). Stripping deps to dodge the check trades away the dependency coupling the check exists to enforce.
- Image-baked SDK: the gateway runs from the sealed Nix venv, not the image's system Python, so it never reaches the import path.
- Source patch + re-instantiate (this workstoday, but is a pain to maintain): add the extra to `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` via `pkgs.applyPatches`, then `callPackage` the package from the patched tree. Required because uv2nix reads the lock at evaluation time, so `overrideAttrs { patches = ...; }` is too late (`patchPhase` runs after the venv set is resolved). It works, but the patch has to be regenerated at each release. The proposed one-line extra removes this entirely.

The one-line extra is strictly simpler than all of these, matches how other dependency groups already work, and changes nothing for non-Nix installs.

See attached files for an example source patch and nix config I'm using as the painful workaround.

[hermes-agent-langfuse-extra.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29106077/hermes-agent-langfuse-extra.patch)

[hermes.nix.example.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29106207/hermes.nix.example.txt)

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

```shell

```

---

## Bug 1: No compression threshold autoraise for `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`

`_compression_threshold_for_model` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` only autoraises the threshold for `gpt-5.5*` models (to 0.85, because its Codex backend caps at 272k). `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` has a **128k context window** (correctly recorded in `model_metadata.py`) but receives no autoraise — it inherits the global default of 0.50.

At 50% of 128k = ~64k tokens, compression fires. But at that point the session may not have accumulated enough messages to have a compressible window (see Bug 2), so compression either skips or fires at the wrong time.

**Relevant code:** `agent/auxiliary_client.py` — `_is_codex_gpt55()` and `_compression_threshold_for_model()`

**Fix:** extend `_compression_threshold_for_model` to cover `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` with an appropriate threshold (e.g. 0.70).

---

## Bug 2: Silent context wipe when `protect_last_n` leaves no compressible window

When compression triggers on a session with few messages, `compress_start >= compress_end` — there is nothing between the protected head and protected tail to summarize. With the default `protect_last_n: 20` and `protect_first_n: 3`, a compressible window requires **at least 25 messages**. Short sessions on a 128k model can hit the token limit with fewer messages than that.

When this happens:
1. Compression is marked ineffective (`_ineffective_compression_count` increments)
2. Context is still over limit
3. No recovery path → the context window gets wiped

This is particularly bad because the user sees no warning — the session just loses its history.

**Relevant code:** `agent/context_compressor.py` lines ~2188-2230

**Fix:** Either (a) add a per-model `protect_last_n` config override, or (b) have the compressor dynamically reduce `protect_last_n` when no compressible window exists rather than failing silently.

---

## Reproduction

1. Use `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` via `openai-codex` provider
2. Run a session with substantial tool output but relatively few message turns (e.g. 15-20 messages, ~90k tokens)
3. Observe: compression triggers, reports "nothing to compress", context is wiped

## Environment

- Provider: `openai-codex`
- Model: `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`
- Context window: 128k
- `compression.protect_last_n`: 20 (default)
- `compression.threshold`: 0.50 (default, no autoraise applied)

items.title: perf: lazy_deps runs the ensurepip→pip bootstrap on every launch for managed/read-only installs (NixOS) — ~20s CPU/start, never persists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/nix
labels.description: Nix flake, NixOS module, container packaging

items.body:
## Summary

On a read-only / package-manager-managed install (NixOS; same class as Homebrew), `tools/lazy_deps.ensure()` is triggered at **startup** for any configured-but-missing backend (e.g. `tts.provider: edge` → `edge-tts`, `stt: local` → `faster-whisper`). The Nix environment ships **no pip**, so `_venv_pip_install` falls all the way to `python -m ensurepip --upgrade --default-pip`, which unpacks and byte-compiles pip from the bundled wheel (~15s CPU via zipimport) before `pip install` then fails against the read-only `/nix/store`. Nothing is cached, and `ensure()` never consults `config.is_managed()`, so **the full bootstrap re-runs on every single launch**, adding ~20s of CPU to startup.

`is_managed()` already exists and returns `True` on NixOS — it just isn't checked here.

## Environment

- Install: NixOS, `hermes-agent` 0.16.0 built via the flake (commit `317c41c`, the #48213 `fix/nix-importnpmlock` branch), env python 3.12.13, `/nix/store/…-hermes-agent-env` (read-only).
- Provider: `openai-codex` (gpt-5.5). Several backends enabled whose deps are not in the derivation (`tts.provider: edge`, `stt.enabled: true` / `provider: local`, …).

## Symptom / measurements

- Time-to-prompt ≈ 35–39 s; **~23 s of it user CPU**, single-threaded.
- `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 hermes` (or `security.allow_lazy_installs: false`): **user CPU 22.9 s → 3.8 s**, wall ≈ 29 s → ≈ 5 s (controlled `time timeout … hermes` runs).
- `python -X importtime` self-time totals only **3.3 s**, so imports are not the cost.

## Profile (py-spy, 21.7k samples)

Subprocess tree captured during the splash:

```
…/bin/hermes
 ├─ …/python3.12 -m ensurepip --upgrade --default-pip
 └─ …/python3.12 -c '… pip install --no-index --find-links /tmp/tmpXXXX --upgrade pip'
```

Hot frames: `subprocess._try_wait` (main thread blocked on the child) and `zipimport._compile_source` / `ast.parse` (pip compiling itself from the wheel). `/tmp/tmpXXXX` is an ephemeral `mkdtemp`, so there is no reuse between launches.

## Root cause (code)

- `tools/lazy_deps.py::ensure()` (≈L432) is called on the first-import path of backends that are configured but whose deps aren't present.
- `_venv_pip_install()` (≈L354): Tier 1 `uv` (absent) → Tier 2 probe `python -m pip` (absent in the Nix env) → `python -m ensurepip --upgrade --default-pip` (≈L394, the expensive step) → `pip install …` which fails on the read-only store.
- `_allow_lazy_installs()` (≈L236) gates on the config flag and `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS`, but **not** on `hermes_cli.config.is_managed()` (≈config.py:L330).
- No negative caching, so a guaranteed-to-fail install is retried in full every launch.

This is the startup/perf counterpart to #30594 (same `_venv_pip_install`, but that one is `hermes update`-time on Debian/PEP 668 where system pip refuses *fast*; on Nix there is no pip, so it pays the ensurepip+compile cost), and it is the root cause behind #27047 (NixOS backend "not installed" — it can't be, and shouldn't be attempted).

## Repro

1. Install via Nix (read-only store, env without pip).
2. Enable a backend whose package isn't in the derivation (e.g. `tts.provider: edge`).
3. Launch `hermes` → ~20 s CPU every start. `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 hermes` is fast.

## Suggested fix

In `ensure()` (or at the top of `_venv_pip_install`), short-circuit when the install can't persist:

- if `config.is_managed()` (NixOS/Homebrew), or the target `site-packages` isn't writable, **skip the install** and raise `FeatureUnavailable` with the managed remediation (point at the flake / `hermes tools`) instead of running ensurepip+pip;
- optionally negative-cache a failed `(feature, version)` for the process lifetime.

This removes ~20 s from every managed-install launch, and gives a clean "add this to your Nix derivation" message instead of a silent, doomed, repeated install (resolving #27047's UX too).

## Workaround

`security.allow_lazy_installs: false` (or `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1`). For Nix users, wrapping the package to also `--set HERMES_MANAGED nixos` additionally stops `hermes update` from fighting the store.

---

Related: #30594, #27047, #36648, #44403.
