items.title: tui_gateway.slash_worker processes are not reaped when their parent session is interrupted mid-compaction

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

`tui_gateway.slash_worker` Python processes are not reliably cleaned up when the session they belong to is interrupted (gateway death, parent-terminal close, mid-compaction cut). They survive across full gateway death-and-rebirth cycles and only get cleared by a manual `taskkill`. While alive, they appear to block the gateway's session subsystem, causing Hermes Desktop to display "offline / reconnecting" status even when the gateway itself is healthy.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (Windows 10, git-bash)
- Gateway listening on `127.0.0.1:8642`
- Active session: `20260618_200347_a0b43f` (MiniMax-M3 model)

## Repro

1. Start an interactive TUI session that uses a slash command (e.g. `/command`).
2. Trigger a hard interruption while the session is mid-compaction — e.g. close the parent terminal, kill the gateway process (`taskkill /F`), or let the session hang unanswered through a long compaction.
3. Restart the gateway with `hermes gateway run`.
4. Inspect the process table.

Expected: the `tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key <key>` processes from the interrupted session are reaped on gateway shutdown or on session-end.

Actual: the slash_worker processes survive the gateway crash and the gateway restart. They only get cleaned up by manual `taskkill /F <pid>`.

## Observed behavior

Process table after gateway restart (Windows `wmic`):

```
python.exe ... -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260618_200347_a0b43f --model MiniMax-M3  (PID 6220)
python.exe ... -m tui_gateway.slash_worker --session-key 20260618_200347_a0b43f --model MiniMax-M3  (PID 22676)
```

Two slash_workers for the same session_key are alive simultaneously, ~2 hours after the session was interrupted.

Gateway startup log on restart shows:

```
INFO gateway.run: Recovered 1 background process(es) from previous run
```

…indicating the gateway *attempts* to recover these, but never actually reaps or completes their lifecycle.

Meanwhile, gateway health endpoint is fully responsive:

```
$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8642/health
{"status": "ok", "platform": "hermes-agent", "version": "0.16.0"}
```

But Hermes Desktop (Electron renderer) shows the status bar as **offline / reconnecting**. After `taskkill /F` on both slash_worker PIDs and a Desktop reload (Ctrl+R), the status bar returns to **connected**. So the live presence of the slash_workers is what's blocking the Desktop IPC path, even though the gateway itself is healthy.

## Root cause hypothesis

`slash_worker` is spawned as a child of the parent TUI session (or the gateway, on its behalf) but its lifecycle is tied to neither. There is no:

1. Cleanup hook fired when the gateway receives SIGTERM/SIGKILL — the children are orphaned to PID 1 or to whatever Windows re-parents them to (the parent terminal's conhost, in our case).
2. Heartbeat / liveness check — a slash_worker for an interrupted session sits idle indefinitely.
3. Reap-on-recovery — `gateway.run`'s "Recovered N background process(es)" line *records* the orphans but does not terminate them, even when the session they belong to has no live owner.

The session JSON itself is correctly persisted (we recovered it via `session_search` and the data is intact), so the bug is specifically the lifetime of the worker process, not the session record.

## Suggested fix

Pick one or both:

1. **Reap orphans on gateway startup.** The "Recovered N background process(es)" path should query the live process list for `tui_gateway.slash_worker` entries whose `session_key` does not match any session currently active on a connected platform, and `os.terminate()` them.
2. **Track the parent PID and reap on parent death.** On Windows, register a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the slash_worker dies when the gateway process exits, even on a hard kill. (Or use a Linux-style PR_SET_PDEATHSIG equivalent — not directly available on Windows, so Job Objects are the right primitive.)

## Workaround (for users)

Until this is fixed, the manual cleanup is:

```bash
wmic process where "name='python.exe'" get ProcessId,CommandLine /format:csv \
  | grep -E "tui_gateway|slash_worker" \
  | awk -F'","' '{print $2}' \
  | awk -F',' '{print $1}' \
  | xargs -I{} taskkill //PID {} //F
```

Then reload Hermes Desktop with Ctrl+R.

## Severity

Medium — recoverable by the user with `taskkill` + Desktop reload, but the symptom (Desktop offline while gateway is healthy) is identical to "the gateway is broken" and burns a lot of triage time before the user figures out the gateway is fine and the orphan workers are the culprit.

items.title: Cron jobs not profile-aware: skills and storage use global paths

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a cron job is created from a **non-default profile** (e.g. `mimo_v25`), it is stored in the **global** cron directory (`~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`) instead of the profile-specific directory (`~/.hermes/profiles/{name}/cron/jobs.json`). Additionally, when the scheduler executes the job, it uses `HERMES_HOME` to resolve skills, which points to the global `~/.hermes/skills/` directory — **not** the profile-specific skills directory.

This means **profile-specific skills attached to cron jobs cannot be found** at execution time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a non-default profile (e.g. `mimo_v25`)
2. Add a skill to that profile only (e.g. `~/.hermes/profiles/mimo_v25/skills/ballejaune-booking/`)
3. Create a cron job from that profile with `skills: ["ballejaune-booking"]`
4. Wait for the job to execute

## Expected Behavior

- Cron job is stored in the profile-specific cron directory
- The scheduler loads skills from the profile-specific skills directory
- The WebUI cron dashboard shows the job

## Actual Behavior

| Component | Path used | Profile-aware? |
|---|---|---|
| `cronjob` tool (writes jobs) | `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json` | No |
| Scheduler (reads + executes) | `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json` | No |
| `skill_view()` in scheduler | `~/.hermes/skills/` | No |
| WebUI cron dashboard | `~/.hermes/profiles/{name}/cron/jobs.json` | Yes |

### Consequences

1. **Skills not found**: The scheduler calls `skill_view("ballejaune-booking")` which searches `~/.hermes/skills/` (via `get_skills_dir()`). If the skill only exists in `~/.hermes/profiles/mimo_v25/skills/`, it returns "skill not found" and the skill is **silently skipped**.
2. **Job invisible in dashboard**: The WebUI reads from the profile-specific cron dir, so jobs created via the tool don't appear in the profile cron dashboard.
3. **Workaround**: Manually copy job entries from `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json` to `~/.hermes/profiles/{name}/cron/jobs.json` — but this only fixes visibility, not skill resolution.

## Root Cause

`cron/jobs.py` resolves paths at module import time:

```python
HERMES_DIR = get_hermes_home().resolve()  # -> ~/.hermes
CRON_DIR = HERMES_DIR / "cron"
JOBS_FILE = CRON_DIR / "jobs.json"
```

And `tools/skills_tool.py` does the same:

```python
HERMES_HOME = get_hermes_home()
SKILLS_DIR = HERMES_HOME / "skills"
```

Neither component is aware of the active profile.

## Suggested Fix

The WebUI already handles this correctly via `_call_cron_for_profile()` which temporarily retargets `cron.jobs` module globals. A similar approach could be applied to:

1. The `cronjob` tool — write to the profile-specific cron dir when invoked from a profile session
2. The scheduler — resolve skills using the profile-specific skills directory
3. Or propagate `HERMES_HOME` as the profile dir when spawning cron subprocesses

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: latest (as of 2026-06-18)
- Profile: `mimo_v25`
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)
- Reference: related to issue #18594 (HERMES_HOME profile propagation)

items.title: observe_unmentioned_group_messages: observed context silently dropped before the API call (early persist mutates the shared messages list)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When `observe_unmentioned_group_messages` is enabled, observed group-chat context that is wrapped into the current user message is silently dropped before the request reaches the model. The model receives the **bare** current message (and the observed rows are also withheld from replay history), so it answers as if it has no context. There is no error and no log line — it fails silently.

Root cause is a shared-mutable-state aliasing bug: the crash-resilience "early persist" in `build_turn_context` calls `_apply_persist_user_message_override`, which mutates `messages[idx]["content"]` **in place** to the bare `persist_user_message`, and it runs **before** `api_messages` is built from that same list.

## Affected versions

Reproduced on `main` (`c2fa302e9`) and on `0.16.0` (`f6416f50f`). The persist-override mechanism is identical across both.

## Mechanism (paths/lines on `main`)

1. `gateway/run.py:15273` — `_api_run_message = _wrap_current_message_with_observed_context(_run_message, observed_group_context)` (observed context wrapped into the message).
2. `gateway/run.py:15283` — because `observed_group_context` is truthy, `persist_user_message = message` (the bare text); then `run_conversation(_api_run_message, persist_user_message=<bare>)`.
3. `agent/conversation_loop.py:407` — `build_turn_context(...)`:
   - `agent/turn_context.py:222` — the **wrapped** message is appended to `messages[idx]`.
   - `agent/turn_context.py:124` — `agent._persist_user_message_override = persist_user_message` (bare); `_persist_user_message_idx` set.
   - `agent/turn_context.py:240` — **unconditional** crash-resilience `agent._persist_session(messages, conversation_history)` (guarded only by `try/except`, no provider/feature gate).
4. `run_agent.py` `_apply_persist_user_message_override` — `messages[idx]["content"] = override` (in-place mutation of the shared list).
5. `agent/conversation_loop.py:527` — `messages = _ctx.messages` (same object); `:714` — `api_msg = msg.copy()` copies the now-**bare** content.

Net: the observed context reaches neither `system`, nor history, nor the current message.

## Reproduction

Config: `require_mention: true` + `observe_unmentioned_group_messages: true` + chat in `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` + the observe channel-prompt marker present.

1. In an allowed group, post a couple of untagged messages (stored with `observed=1`).
2. @-mention the bot with a message that refers to them (e.g. "what do you think of this?").
3. The bot replies as if it has no context / no subject.

## Evidence (captured request bodies via `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1`)

Preflight body of the triggered turn:

- The untagged lines appear **nowhere** in the request — not in `system`, not in `messages`, not in the current user message (`system` length ~33.7k).
- The same lines are present in `state.db` with `observed=1`. **Capture works; only delivery fails.**
- For contrast, delivering the observed block via the system prompt instead makes the same lines appear in `system` (length ~44.7k) and the model engages — isolating the failure to the in-place strip on the message path.

## Why CI is green

The delivery unit tests in `tests/gateway/test_telegram_group_gating.py` exercise `_build_gateway_agent_history` / `_wrap_current_message_with_observed_context` in isolation; none run the full `run_conversation` path where the early persist mutates the shared list. The end-to-end seam is untested.

## Suggested fix

Make `_apply_persist_user_message_override` operate on a copy for persistence (copy-on-persist) instead of mutating the shared `messages` list — or skip the override on the prologue/early persist and apply it only on terminal persistence paths. That decouples "keep the DB transcript clean" from "what the API request is built from."

items.title: Desktop app doesn't show Telegram session messages in real-time

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes desktop app (Electron) loads a Telegram session from the SQLite DB history but **does not update with new messages in real-time**. The session appears in the session list and historical messages render, but any new messages sent via Telegram after the desktop app opened never appear.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Telegram conversation with the Hermes gateway (send a few messages)
2. Open the Hermes desktop app (`open Hermes.app` or `hermes desktop`)
3. Navigate to the Telegram session in the session picker — historical messages load correctly
4. Send a new message via Telegram
5. Observe: the message never appears in the desktop app UI (it does arrive in Telegram correctly)

## Expected Behavior

The desktop app should show new messages from Telegram sessions in real-time, just like it does for local TUI/desktop sessions.

## Actual Behavior

- Historical messages from the Telegram session load from the DB ✅
- New messages sent via Telegram after the app opened **never appear** ❌
- The desktop app WebSocket disconnects frequently (code 1012 — service restart) and the dashboard backend restarts every ~2 minutes, creating a new port each time (63891 → 52151 → 52779 → 53314 → 53445 → 54030)
- The gateway process (`gateway run --replace`) and the dashboard process are separate — the desktop app WebSocket connects to the **dashboard**, not the **gateway**, so it never receives Telegram platform events

## Root Cause Analysis

From inspecting the source code (`apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts`):

1. The desktop app connects its WebSocket to the **dashboard backend** (local Python `web_server`)
2. Telegram messages are handled by the **gateway** (`hermes_cli.main gateway run`) — a completely separate process
3. The dashboard backend does not forward gateway/platform events (Telegram messages) to the desktop WebSocket
4. The desktop app has auto-reconnect logic with backoff (1s→2s→4s...→15s) but even when the WS reconnects, it only syncs local sessions — it never subscribes to gateway platform events
5. The repeated dashboard restarts (code 1012) compound the issue: each restart loses the WS connection, and the session view does not recover the Telegram session live state

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 26.5.1 (Apple Silicon)
- **Hermes Agent:** v0.16.0 (up to date, upstream 03d9a95a)
- **Desktop app:** Electron, `apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app`
- **Model:** glm-5.2:cloud via Ollama (local `ollama serve` at 127.0.0.1:11434)
- **Platform:** Telegram DM
- **Launch method tested:** `ollama launch hermes-desktop` AND direct `open Hermes.app` — same behavior in both cases

## Logs

Gateway logs show Telegram messages arriving and being processed correctly:
```
2026-06-18 17:01:52 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=telegram user=emmanuel_sd chat=914698290 msg=...
2026-06-18 17:01:39 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=telegram chat=914698290 time=5.5s
```

GUI logs show WebSocket disconnect/reconnect cycles:
```
2026-06-18 16:57:31 WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws send failed peer=127.0.0.1:53452 error_type=WebSocketDisconnect
2026-06-18 17:00:52 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:54036
```

## Suggested Approach

The dashboard backend (or the desktop app's WebSocket handler) needs to subscribe to gateway platform events and forward them to the renderer, so messages from Telegram (and other messaging platforms) appear in real-time. Alternatively, the desktop app could connect to the gateway's event stream directly for non-local sessions.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes update on system Python targets wrong interpreter and hits PEP 668 (no-venv + uv branch)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug

`hermes update` (the main install path, not the lazy-deps refresh) fails on macOS with Homebrew Python 3.14 and silently targets the wrong Python / gets blocked by PEP 668. Two real bugs in `hermes_cli/main.py::_cmd_update_pip`'s "no-venv + uv" branch:

1. `uv pip install --system` defaults to the **first** system Python on PATH, not the interpreter hermes is actually running under. On a multi-Python Mac (`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13` + Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/...`), this installs 0.16.0 to Python 3.13 — a prefix that no hermes binary on the user's PATH actually uses. Result: the upgrade appears to succeed but `hermes --version` keeps reporting the old version.

2. When the active interpreter IS the right one (Homebrew Python 3.14), uv hits the `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker (PEP 668) and refuses to install. No `--break-system-packages` is passed.

This is the **same root cause** as #30594 (lazy-deps path) and the now-closed #2648 (original main-path fix), but a different function in a different module. The 0.16.0 partial fix added `--system` to the no-venv branch but didn't pin the Python target or handle PEP 668.

## Repro

macOS, Homebrew Python 3.14.4, hermes-agent 0.15.2 installed via `pip install --break-system-packages` directly into `/opt/homebrew/lib/python3.14/site-packages/` (no venv, no pipx). `uv` present at `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`.

```
$ which hermes
/opt/homebrew/bin/hermes

$ hermes update
⚕ Updating Hermes Agent...

→ Current version: 0.15.2
→ Checking PyPI for updates...
→ Running: /opt/homebrew/bin/uv pip install --upgrade hermes-agent
✗ Update failed
```

Underlying error (visible only with `uv --verbose`): `error: No virtual environment found; run \`uv venv\` to create an environment, or pass \`--system\` to install into a non-virtual environment`. That's the pre-0.16.0 failure mode.

After upgrading to 0.16.0 the same call now produces this on the user's machine:

```
Using Python 3.13.2 environment at: /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13
```

`uv` silently picked Python 3.13 (the first system Python on PATH), not the Python 3.14 that the active `hermes` binary actually uses. `--system` was added but `--python` was not pinned, and there's no PEP 668 override.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/main.py::_cmd_update_pip` (current `main` branch, function lines ~10181-10202):

```python
elif uv:
    cmd = [uv, "pip", "install", "--upgrade", "hermes-agent"]
    if in_venv:
        export_virtualenv = True
    else:
        # Outside any venv, ``--system`` lets uv target the active
        # interpreter, matching pip's default behaviour.
        cmd.insert(3, "--system")
```

Two problems with the `else` branch:

- `--system` alone lets uv pick the first system Python on PATH, not `sys.executable`. macOS users with both framework Python and Homebrew Python get the wrong target.
- No `--break-system-packages` is passed, so PEP 668-protected system Pythons (Homebrew's `python@3.14`, Debian/Ubuntu, Kali) reject the install.

## Suggested fix

Pin `--python` to `sys.executable` and pass `--break-system-packages` for the no-venv + uv case:

```python
elif uv:
    cmd = [uv, "pip", "install", "--upgrade", "hermes-agent"]
    if in_venv:
        export_virtualenv = True
    else:
        # Outside any venv, ``--system`` lets uv target the active
        # interpreter, matching pip's default behaviour.  Pin to
        # ``sys.executable`` because uv's --system default is the
        # FIRST system Python it finds, which on a multi-Python Mac
        # is /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13 —
        # not the interpreter hermes is actually running under
        # (e.g. Homebrew's python@3.14).
        cmd.insert(3, "--system")
        cmd.insert(3, "--python")
        cmd.insert(4, sys.executable)
        # System Pythons ship an EXTERNALLY-MANAGED marker (PEP 668)
        # which blocks pip writes by default.  For hermes — which is
        # itself a pip-installed CLI tool that needs to upgrade in
        # place — ``--break-system-packages`` is the right call.
        # A pipx/uv-tool/venv install never reaches this branch
        # (those branches are handled above), so the flag is safe
        # to apply unconditionally in the no-venv + uv case.
        cmd.insert(5, "--break-system-packages")
else:
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "--upgrade",
           "--break-system-packages", "hermes-agent"]
```

The `else` branch (no `uv` on PATH) also needs `--break-system-packages` for parity.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.3.1
- Python: 3.14.4 (Homebrew, externally-managed)
- Hermes: 0.15.2 → 0.16.0 (verified both pre- and post-0.16.0-failure)
- Install method: `pip install --break-system-packages` into Homebrew Python 3.14 system prefix
- uv: present (`/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`)

## Workaround (until fixed)

Install via `pipx` (recommended for any system-Python install):

```bash
pipx install --python /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 hermes-agent  # pin to <3.14
```

`pipx upgrade hermes-agent` then works forever. The `_cmd_update_pip` function already detects pipx-managed installs and routes through `pipx upgrade`. Users who can't switch to pipx can manually upgrade with:

```bash
uv pip install --python /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14 \
               --system --break-system-packages --upgrade hermes-agent
```

## Related

- #30594 — same root cause, but in `tools/lazy_deps.py::_venv_pip_install` (lazy-deps refresh path)
- #2648 — closed, original PEP 668 fix for the main `hermes update` path (only covered a partial scenario; this issue covers the gaps left when the function was restructured to handle the `is_uv_tool_install()` / `pipx_managed` cases)

## Notes on scope

The pipx migration is the durable answer for users hitting this; the function-level fix is for users who can't or don't want to switch install methods. Both are worth doing.

---
**Suggested labels:** `type/bug`, `comp/cli`, `P2`, `python:uv`

items.title: Startup perf/UX: bundled Teams/Discord platform plugins should be first-level opt-in

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Opinionated feedback / startup-performance bug: bundled gateway platform plugins are treated as "available out of the box" by auto-loading their adapters for everyone. That makes Discord and especially Teams part of first-use startup even for users who never asked for them.

This feels like the wrong opt-in boundary:

- Current behavior: platform adapter is loaded by default, then credentials/config decide whether it actually connects.
- Desired behavior: platform integration itself is the first opt-in; credentials/config are the second opt-in after the user chooses that platform.

In other words: Discord/Teams should be manifest-visible and easy to enable, but not imported/registered as live platform adapters until asked for or minimally configured.

## Why this matters

Most Hermes users are not using every messaging platform all the time. Auto-loading all bundled platform adapters assumes everyone uses Discord and Teams all the time. For first-use / CLI / single-platform users, it adds cold-start cost and makes the plugin model feel backwards: "available out of the box" should mean discoverable in setup/status, not eagerly imported into the runtime.

This is adjacent to, but not identical to, #31109. #31109 is about an explicit disable being ignored by platform auto-enable. This report is about the default design: bundled platform plugins are auto-loaded before the user has opted into that platform at all.

## Measured example

On my macOS Hermes install, fresh Python process plugin discovery:

- Default bundled platform plugin load: about 504-543 ms
- Disable Discord only: about 478-498 ms
- Disable Teams only: about 196-198 ms
- Disable both Discord and Teams: about 171-193 ms

So the avoidable cold-start cost is roughly 0.33s in this setup, mostly from the Teams platform adapter import path. Once warm in-process, discovery is effectively free, but the cold-start/first-use path is what users feel.

I also checked that this is not model tool-schema bloat in my current config:

- CLI prompt-size tools: 33 tools / 62,488 tool-schema bytes
- Simulated Discord platform prompt-size: 33 tools / 62,488 tool-schema bytes
- Simulated Teams platform prompt-size: 33 tools / 62,488 tool-schema bytes
- No `discord*` or `teams*` model tools were present in the active model-facing tool list

So the issue here is gateway/plugin startup behavior, not per-turn tool-schema overhead.

## Current implementation shape observed

`hermes_cli/plugins.py` treats bundled `kind: platform` plugins like built-in support and auto-loads them:

```python
if manifest.source == "bundled" and manifest.kind in {"backend", "platform"}:
    self._load_plugin(manifest)
    continue
```

That imports adapter modules like:

- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`
- `plugins/platforms/teams/adapter.py`

Teams in particular pulls in the Teams SDK path during module import if installed/configured in the environment, and even when it does not connect, the adapter has already been paid for.

## Desired behavior

Keep platforms discoverable without importing them eagerly:

1. Read `plugin.yaml` manifests cheaply at startup.
2. Show platform availability from manifest metadata:
   - `Discord: available, not configured`
   - `Microsoft Teams: available, not configured`
3. Import/register the heavy adapter module only when one of these is true:
   - the user runs platform setup for that platform
   - required env/config is present
   - the platform is explicitly enabled in config
   - the gateway is actually starting that platform
   - a platform-specific status/test command needs the adapter

A status display could look like:

```text
Discord: available (not loaded; missing DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN)
Microsoft Teams: available (not loaded; missing TEAMS_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/TENANT_ID)
Teams pipeline: disabled
```

## Why I think this is a bug, not just an enhancement

The current behavior makes "bundled" mean "paid for on startup" rather than "available to configure." For heavyweight integrations, that is a UX/performance bug. It also creates confusing second-level opt-in semantics: a user has not opted into Teams just because Hermes ships a Teams adapter.

The first opt-in should be the platform. Credentials are the second opt-in.

## Suggested implementation direction

Add a manifest-only platform registry entry or lazy platform descriptor:

- manifest scan registers lightweight metadata only
- setup/status can list the platform from metadata
- runtime/gateway imports the adapter only when config/env says it should be active
- explicit `plugins.disabled` and `platforms.<name>.enabled: false` remain hard stops

This would preserve "out of the box" setup discoverability without charging every user the import/startup cost for platforms they never use.

## Repro / benchmark sketch

The rough measurement I used was a fresh-process plugin discovery under a temp `HERMES_HOME`, comparing default config to temp configs with:

```yaml
plugins:
  disabled:
    - discord-platform
    - teams-platform
```

and variants disabling only one of the two. The exact numbers will vary by machine and installed optional deps, but the shape is the important part: Teams/Discord are being imported before platform opt-in.

items.title: Bug: delegate_task(background=true) is advertised for long-running work but hard-times out at 600s

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

`delegate_task(background=true)` is advertised to the model as the right primitive for "long-running independent work", but in practice the child is still killed at the default 600s timeout and returns no partial summary. This is a prompt/tool-contract bug, not just a timeout-length feature request: Hermes' own tool description steers the agent into a path that fails under normal real work.

In my session, the agent followed the tool prompt and dispatched background subagents for independent research/coding lanes. Two returned exactly at ~600s with `status=timeout`; a third had to be salvaged manually. The parent then had to inspect worktrees/logs, close stale claims, and reconstruct artifacts itself.

The most frustrating bit: the prompt said this was the right tool. The system default broke itself.

## Relevant Tool Contract Excerpt

The model-facing `delegate_task` description currently contains both of these ideas:

- do not use delegation for durable long-running work that must outlive the current turn; use cron/terminal background instead
- `background=true`: "Run the subagent asynchronously in the BACKGROUND... Use for long-running independent work... Do NOT poll or wait after dispatching — just continue; the result will come to you."

Those are in tension. The second statement is what the agent acted on. The implementation reality is that the subagent can still die at `delegation.child_timeout_seconds` (600s default), and the parent receives only a timeout summary after the work is gone.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Hermes CLI, ask the agent to fan out several independent research/coding tasks that require repository reading, small implementation, verification, and a written artifact.
2. Let Hermes choose `delegate_task(background=true)` based on the tool description.
3. Wait for the background completion event.
4. Observe that children time out after 600 seconds, even when they were doing bounded but non-trivial work.

## Actual Behavior

Observed completion messages:

```text
Status: timeout   API calls: 50   Duration: 600.01s
Subagent timed out after 600.0s with 50 API call(s) completed — likely stuck on a slow API call or unresponsive network request.

Status: timeout   API calls: 44   Duration: 600.02s
Subagent timed out after 600.0s with 44 API call(s) completed — likely stuck on a slow API call or unresponsive network request.
```

Impact in the concrete run:

- One subagent actually wrote code and completed short offline runs, but timed out before closeout/reporting. Parent had to recover logs manually.
- One subagent produced no discoverable worktree/log/report before timeout.
- One subagent was killed during/after a long run, leaving partial evidence and stale coordination state.
- The parent saw no partial transcript, no artifact manifest, no heartbeat summary, and no structured "what I changed before timeout" payload.
- Claims/coordination state remained active until parent manually cleaned it up.

## Expected Behavior

One of these should be true:

1. `delegate_task(background=true)` is genuinely durable/background-capable:
   - timeout is configurable per call or clearly much longer for background tasks,
   - task survives parent turn interruption where possible,
   - parent can list/status/collect/cancel,
   - timeout returns partial transcript / last heartbeat / artifact manifest,
   - subagent is encouraged or required to journal progress before long operations.

or:

2. The model-facing prompt/schema must stop advertising it as suitable for long-running independent work:
   - explicitly say `background=true` still has a 600s default child timeout,
   - say it is for short async work only,
   - tell the model to use `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)`, cron, kanban, or a spawned Hermes process for anything likely to exceed a few minutes,
   - add a planning heuristic: if the delegated task includes repo discovery + implementation + tests/runs + report, split it or don't use delegate_task.

## Why This Is Not Just "Increase the Timeout"

A longer timeout helps, but the bug is the mismatch between the model-facing affordance and runtime semantics. The prompt says "long-running independent work" and "do not poll"; the runtime says "hard kill at 600s, no partials". That contradiction causes the agent to make the wrong orchestration choice by default.

This overlaps with timeout/configuration issues, but the fix needs to include prompt/schema changes and better failure semantics, not only a bigger number.

## Suggested Fixes

Opinionated proposal:

- Rename or reword background delegation as "short async subtask" unless/until it is durable.
- Add `timeout_seconds` to `delegate_task` or expose `delegation.child_timeout_seconds` in a way the model can reason about.
- Add a mandatory periodic child heartbeat journal that gets returned on timeout.
- On timeout, return:
  - last assistant message / last N tool calls,
  - files modified or created if known,
  - current workdir,
  - active background processes spawned by the child,
  - child todo state if available.
- Add `delegate_status`, `delegate_collect`, `delegate_cancel`, `delegate_log` tools for background tasks, or route users to kanban/cron/terminal background instead.
- Update the tool description so the model does not choose this path for 10+ minute research/code lanes.

## Environment

```text
Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
upstream 28d887ca
local d1228816 (+1 carried commit)
Python: 3.11.15 inside Hermes
OS: macOS / Darwin arm64
```

## Related Existing Issues

Likely related, but this report is specifically about the prompt/tool-contract mismatch:

- #42861 — configurable/increased subagent timeout
- #47302 — synchronous/stuck subagent freezes parent turn
- #5586 — non-blocking background agent delegation

items.title: [Bug]: Hermes Desktop on Windows — clicking notification shows "session not found"
items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows, when Hermes Desktop receives a new message notification and the user clicks it (either from Windows Action Center or the toast popup), the app focuses but fails to navigate to the correct conversation, displaying **"session not found"** instead.

The notification click is supposed to send the user to the relevant chat session, but the session ID appears to be stale or the routing fails on Windows specifically.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Desktop on Windows 11
2. Connect a messaging platform (e.g. WeChat/Telegram) via Gateway
3. Minimize Hermes Desktop to system tray / background
4. Receive a new message from a platform contact - Windows notification toast appears
5. **Click** the notification toast to focus Hermes Desktop
6. The app window comes to front, but the correct chat session is not loaded
7. An error message appears: **"session not found"** or the app lands on a blank/default view instead of the correct conversation

## Expected Behavior

Clicking a notification should:
- Focus the Hermes Desktop window
- Navigate to the specific chat session that generated the notification
- Display the conversation history and new message

## Actual Behavior

- The window focuses correctly (via `focusWindow()`)
- But the `hermes:focus-session` IPC message either:
  - Carries a stale/expired sessionId
  - The session routing in the renderer fails to resolve the session
  - Or the session list has not been fully loaded when the focus event arrives

## Root Cause Analysis

The notification handler is in `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` (lines 5629-5655):

```js
notification.on('click', () => {
  if (!mainWindow || mainWindow.isDestroyed()) return
  focusWindow(mainWindow)
  if (payload?.sessionId) {
    mainWindow.webContents.send('hermes:focus-session', payload.sessionId)
  }
})
```

And `hermes:focus-session` is bridged through `preload.cjs` (lines 98-101) to the renderer:

```js
onFocusSession: callback => {
  const listener = (_event, sessionId) => callback(sessionId)
  ipcRenderer.on('hermes:focus-session', listener)
  return () => ipcRenderer.removeListener('hermes:focus-session', listener)
}
```

**Likely causes on Windows:**

1. **Windows notification persistence**: Windows Action Center caches notifications even when the app is in the background or has been closed and reopened. When clicked, the `sessionId` in the notification payload may reference a session that was tied to a previous gateway connection or backend process that has since been recycled.

2. **Race condition**: When Hermes Desktop is minimized/backgrounded and the notification triggers a window focus, the renderer may not have finished reconnecting to the gateway backend or reloading the session list. The `focus-session` event arrives before the session registry is populated, so the session ID cannot be resolved.

3. **Session lifecycle mismatch**: On macOS, Electron's notification `click` event fires with a fresh reference to the `Notification` object that was created when the notification was shown. On Windows, the click may come from Action Center replay — reusing a notification object whose `payload` context is serialized/deserialized differently.

## Affected Component

Desktop (Electron app)

## Operating System

Windows 11

## Hermes Version

Latest (v0.16.x+)

## Additional Context

The issue may also be related to how the Gateway backend handles session persistence when the desktop app transitions between foreground/background states on Windows. The session ID routing in the renderer (`onFocusSession` to React router) should be verified to handle late-arriving focus events gracefully.

A proposed mitigation: in the renderer's `onFocusSession` handler, if the session list is not yet loaded, queue the sessionId and retry navigation once sessions are available (rather than failing immediately with "session not found").

# Telegram rich-message streaming renders poorly on Telegram Desktop

## Summary

When `platforms.telegram.extra.rich_messages: true` (the default), Hermes streams responses via `sendRichMessageDraft` + edits in place. This works correctly on Telegram iOS and Android, but **Telegram Desktop either silently drops or fails to render the final message** in some flows. The user sees the bot responding (typing indicators fire, API calls return HTTP 200) but the actual messages never appear on the desktop client. The same bot responses are visible and intact on the iOS app.

This is **not a Telegram Bot API failure** — every sendRichMessageDraft / sendRichMessage / sendMessage call returns HTTP 200 OK. It's a client-side rendering / edit-handling issue with Telegram Desktop specifically.

## Reproduction

1. Install Hermes with default config (`rich_messages: true`)
2. Send the bot a question that triggers a long streamed response (>500 chars)
3. Watch the response stream in via the API logs (every sendRichMessageDraft returns 200 OK, final sendMessage returns 200 OK)
4. Open the same chat in **Telegram Desktop**
5. Bot's messages either:
   - never appear at all (most common)
   - appear briefly then disappear
   - appear as empty/placeholder bubbles

iOS/Android clients receive and render every message correctly.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (post #46890 "edit streamed previews in place as rich")
- python-telegram-bot: current stable
- Telegram Bot API: 10.1+ (rich messages endpoint live)
- Telegram Desktop: tested across recent stable releases
- Telegram iOS: works correctly
- Bot: `Hermes_Helix_Bot` (id 8799129667)
- DM chat_id: 6957322540

## Log evidence

Successful API path (the bot thinks it delivered):

```
2026-06-19 14:11:42,404 INFO httpx: POST .../sendChatAction "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
2026-06-19 14:11:53,203 INFO httpx: POST .../sendRichMessageDraft "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
2026-06-19 14:11:54,254 INFO httpx: POST .../sendRichMessageDraft "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
2026-06-19 14:11:55,836 INFO httpx: POST .../sendRichMessageDraft "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
2026-06-19 14:11:56,384 INFO httpx: POST .../sendMessage "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
2026-06-19 14:11:57,367 INFO gateway.run: Suppressing normal final send ... content_delivered=True
```

User reports seeing none of these in Telegram Desktop, all of them in iOS app.

## Current state

- `platforms.telegram.extra.rich_messages: false` exists as an all-or-nothing opt-out (per-process, line 428 of `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`)
- `_rich_draft_disabled` runtime latch exists (line 433) — flips to `True` after a `sendRichMessageDraft` API failure so later drafts skip the rich attempt
- No client-detection mechanism; no per-chat opt-out; no slash command toggle

## Desired behaviour

Option A (preferred): **per-chat runtime toggle**

Add a `/rich` slash command that flips rich messages on/off for the current chat, persisted across gateway restarts. Users on Telegram Desktop can run `/rich off` once and the bot switches that chat to standard `sendMessage` only, while keeping rich streaming enabled for users on iOS/Android.

Option B: **chat_id allowlist/blocklist in config**

```yaml
telegram:
  extra:
    rich_messages: true   # default
    rich_messages_clients:
      disable_chats: ["-1001234567890"]   # chats where rich gets skipped
```

Option C: **heuristic auto-detection**

Watch for failure patterns from `sendRichMessageDraft` edits (e.g. `Bad Request: message is not modified` after a no-op edit, suggesting the client discarded an intermediate frame) and latch off rich messages for that chat. More fragile than A or B but requires zero user action.

## Why this matters

Rich streaming is a visible quality-of-life feature on iOS/Android — responses feel live and responsive. Forcing it off globally punishes mobile users to accommodate desktop. Per-chat toggle lets users self-select based on their preferred client without losing the feature for everyone.

## Workaround today

```yaml
telegram:
  extra:
    rich_messages: false
```

Global opt-out — works on every client but loses the streaming effect on iOS/Android too.

## Description

When typing `/goal <text>` in the TUI desktop app (Hermes Desktop GUI), the message is silently swallowed and the app returns **"empty command"** (空指令). The user loses whatever text they typed after `/goal`.

This also potentially affects other commands listed in `_PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS`: `retry`, `queue`, `q`, `steer`, `plan`, `undo`.

## Root Cause

The `slash.exec` handler in `tui_gateway/server.py` checks whether the command base is in `_PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS` (line 7679, which includes `goal`). If so, it returns error `4018` instructing the frontend to fall back to `command.dispatch`. Under some conditions the fallback fails, leaving `params.get("command", "")` empty, hitting the guard at line 8926:

```python
if not cmd:
    return _err(rid, 4004, "empty command")
```

The full `/goal <text>` input is lost with no actionable error.

## Affected Files

- `tui_gateway/server.py` line 7679 (`_PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS` includes `goal`)
- `tui_gateway/server.py` line 8918-8940 (`slash.exec` handler rejects pending-input commands)
- `tui_gateway/server.py` line 8926 (empty-command error return point)
- `tui_gateway/server.py` line 7997-8066 (`command.dispatch` `/goal` handler - correct implementation exists)

## Suggested Fix

Instead of returning an error from `slash.exec` for `_PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS`, internally forward to `command.dispatch` by parsing the base command and args, then routing to the same handler. This removes the frontend fallback dependency.

items.title: Desktop "Update" button hangs forever on Windows due to Electron file lock (EBUSY)
items.body:
## Summary

The "Update" button in the Hermes Desktop GUI spawns `hermes-setup.exe`, which attempts a full desktop rebuild via `npm run pack`. On Windows, this hangs indefinitely because the running Electron process holds an exclusive lock on `node_modules\electron`, causing npm to fail with `EBUSY` — and the updater never recovers.

## Symptoms

1. Open Hermes Desktop GUI
2. Click the "Update" button (or the auto-update prompt)
3. A progress spinner appears and **never finishes** — no error, no timeout, no fallback dialog
4. The user must kill `hermes-setup.exe` manually via Task Manager

From `bootstrap-installer.log`:
```
npm error EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rmdir '...node_modules\electron'
npm error EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rename '...node_modules\electron' -> '...\.electron-*'
```

## Root Cause

The issue is architectural: **Hermes Desktop treats a source build as the user-facing update pathway**, unlike every other major Electron application.

### How it breaks

```
[User clicks "Update"]
    ↓
Hermes Desktop (Hermes.exe) spawns hermes-setup.exe
    ↓
hermes-setup.exe: git pull → uv sync → npm ci (root workspace)
    ↓
npm ci tries to clean-install node_modules/electron
    ↓
Windows: EBUSY: resource busy or locked — Electron binary is IN USE by the running Hermes Desktop
    ↓
npm retries → fails again → hermes-setup.exe hangs forever
```

On POSIX, unlinking a running executable works. On Windows, it does not — the file cannot be deleted or renamed while in use. Since the updater is spawned BY the Electron process whose files it needs to replace, the lock can never be released.

### Why it differs from normal Electron apps

| | VS Code / Discord / Chrome | Hermes Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Update delivery | Pre-built binary from CDN | **Builds from source** (git pull → tsc → vite → electron-builder) |
| Lock avoidance | Download to staging dir, swap on restart | `npm ci` in-place — tries to delete locked `node_modules/electron` |
| Toolchain needed | None (download only) | Node.js, npm, TypeScript, Vite, tsc, Python, uv |
| Update time | ~5 seconds | 3-5 minutes |

### Two independent code paths that disagree

Hermes has **two separate update build paths** that handle the desktop build differently:

1. **`hermes-setup.exe`** (Rust binary, spawned by the Desktop GUI) — does NOT know how to terminate the parent Electron process before building, so it hits the file lock and hangs silently.

2. **`hermes desktop --force-build`** (Python CLI) — has `_stop_desktop_processes_locking_build()` (line 5220 in `hermes_cli/main.py`) which uses `psutil` to terminate any `Hermes.exe` running from `release/win-unpacked/` before rebuilding. This path is **never invoked** by the GUI's update button.

The Python code proves the developers understood the Windows lock issue and wrote a fix — but only for the CLI path, not for the Rust updater spawned by the GUI.

## Expected Behavior

The GUI update button should either:

**A.** Work without hanging — download a pre-built binary (standard Electron update pattern), or at minimum delegate to `hermes desktop --force-build` which handles process termination correctly.

**B.** Fail gracefully — detect that the desktop is running and show a clear message: "Desktop app is running. Please close it and restart the update." Not an infinite spinner.

## Suggested Fixes

### Option 1 (recommended): Switch to pre-built binary delivery

Stop building the desktop from source during updates. The CI should produce a packaged installer and upload it to GitHub Releases; the desktop app should use a standard Electron auto-updater (`electron-updater` / Squirrel) to download and stage it.

This eliminates:
- The 3-5 minute source build on every update
- The Node.js toolchain requirement for end users
- The Windows file lock problem entirely
- The dual-codebase split (Rust updater vs Python CLI)

### Option 2: Make the GUI button delegate to the working CLI path

Instead of spawning `hermes-setup.exe`, the Electron main process could spawn `hermes desktop --force-build` (the Python path) in a hidden terminal window. The Python path already handles process termination correctly.

### Option 3: Add process kill + graceful fallback to hermes-setup.exe

If Option 1 is too large, at minimum:
- `hermes-setup.exe` should detect that the Electron process it came from is still running and either kill it before starting npm install (like the Python path does), or print a clear error and exit with a non-zero code instead of hanging
- The Desktop GUI should show a real error state (not an infinite spinner) when the updater exits with failure

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes Desktop:** Latest from `main` (commit c02192ff6)
- **Desktop toolchain:** Node.js v22.22.3, npm 10.x, Python 3.11.15, uv 0.11.22
- **Installed via:** Standalone Hermes Desktop installer
- **Previous related issue:** #46755 (staged updater not found after CLI rebuild — same underlying "build from source instead of download" architectural problem)

## Related

- #46755 — Desktop "Update" button falls back to "run hermes update from terminal" dialog
- `hermes_cli/main.py` lines 5220-5500 — `_stop_desktop_processes_locking_build()` exists for the Python CLI path, confirming the team understands the Windows lock issue but the Rust updater doesn't use it

items.title: Compression-induced duplicate actions: agent re-executes side-effecting operations after context compaction

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

After context compression in long sessions, the agent re-executes side-effecting operations (sending Slack messages, creating PRs, posting to channels) that already succeeded earlier in the conversation.

### What happens

1. User asks agent to send a message (e.g. Slack update to a teammate)
2. Agent sends it successfully
3. Session grows long, compression fires
4. Compressed summary retains the *topic* but loses the fact that the action was *already completed*
5. Agent treats it as an open task and sends the message **again** — duplicate to a real person

### Root cause

Two interacting factors:

1. **Summary quality**: The compressor template has `## Completed Actions` vs `## Pending User Asks` sections, but categorization is entirely LLM-dependent. The summarizer can misclassify completed actions as pending, especially when the agent wrote verbose recap responses that re-stated the task.

2. **No action dedup guard**: There is no programmatic mechanism to prevent re-execution of side-effecting operations after compression. Even if the summary correctly lists an action as completed, there is nothing stopping the agent from re-executing it if it interprets the post-compression context as requiring it.

### Why this is distinct from #19649

PR #19649 improves summary quality to reduce "repeats already-completed work." That helps with *planning/thinking* recycling. But this issue is about **idempotency of real-world actions** — sending messages, creating resources, posting to external systems. Even with better summaries, the risk remains unless there is a hard guard against re-executing actions that already succeeded.

### Observed impact

- Duplicate Slack messages sent to teammates
- Same topic re-raised 3-4 times in a single long session despite being resolved
- User frustration and trust erosion

### Suggested approaches

- **Action log in compression metadata**: Track side-effecting tool calls (send_message, Slack API posts, PR creation, etc.) with their results in a structured format that survives compression — not as natural language the summarizer can misinterpret, but as a programmatic list the agent checks before re-executing.
- **Pre-action dedup check**: Before executing any side-effecting tool call, check whether an equivalent call already succeeded in the current session (even across compression boundaries).
- **Temporal anchoring enforcement**: The compressor prompt already has temporal anchoring instructions ("rewrite completed actions as dated past-tense facts") but enforcement is LLM-dependent. A post-processing validation step could verify completed actions are actually in past tense.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent (latest, running on macOS via gateway)
- Claude Opus 4.8 as primary model
- Long sessions (50+ messages) with multiple compression passes
- Compression config: threshold 0.5, target_ratio 0.2, protect_last_n 20

items.title: [Bug]: Role alternation violation (Tool -> User) when interrupting via /stop leads to model hallucinations and user message continuation

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description
Role alternation violation (`Tool` message followed directly by `User` message) occurs when a session is interrupted via `/stop` after a tool execution, but before the assistant generates a final text response. Because no `assistant` message is appended, the next user message violates strict alternation, causing chat completions API models (like Gemini and Claude) to hallucinate by continuing the user's message in their style/format (including injected timestamps) and generating statements or approvals the user never actually wrote, before eventually transitioning to the assistant persona.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a turn that triggers a tool (e.g. file editing or running code).
2. Let the tool execute successfully (so the `tool` role message is appended to the transcript).
3. Interrupt the turn immediately using the `/stop` command before the assistant streams any text answer.
4. Send a new user message (e.g., "forget it").
5. The model's response will begin by hallucinating and continuing the user's message itself, copying its style, format (often including gateway-injected timestamps), and generating approvals/text that the user never actually intended or wrote, before eventually starting its own assistant analysis.

## Expected Behavior
The conversation history sent to the API must maintain strict role alternation. If an interruption leaves an orphan `tool` message at the tail, a dummy `assistant` message showing the interruption must be inserted to close the transaction.

## Actual Behavior
An invalid sequence is compiled:
`... -> Assistant (tool_calls) -> Tool (success) -> User (new message)`
This violates the strict OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini alternation rules, driving the model into character-mimicry hallucinations and message continuation.

## Relationship to existing items
- Related to #43936 / PR #43962. However, PR #43962 only backfills *visible* delivered text. It does not resolve alternation violations when the interruption occurs on empty/non-started assistant text after a tool run.

## Proposed Fix
Update `repair_message_sequence` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` to detect `Tool -> User` transitions and insert a fallback `assistant` placeholder (e.g., `{"role": "assistant", "content": "Operation interrupted."}`) to cleanly close the tool transaction.

items.title: feat(delegation): shadow_clone SQLite persistence — in-flight tracking survives gateway restart

labels.name: duplicate

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Root cause

`delegate_task(background=true)` (shadow_clone) tasks track their in-flight state in process memory only. A gateway restart loses every pending shadow clone result — the subagent's answer is delivered to no one.

## Diagnosis

`tools/async_delegation.py` keeps a dict of running delegations in RAM. `gateway/run.py` has no durability layer. After restart, `_drain_completion_notifications` never fires the shadow_clone branch for those rows because the in-memory records are gone.

## Proposed fix

Add a `shadow_clone_tasks` table to `SessionDB` (SQLite) and wire write points at dispatch + finalization. On gateway startup, recover in-flight rows (2 h TTL) and GC old terminal rows (24 h retention). Four correctness fixes applied directly:

- **C1** — `asyncio.Lock` per delegation_id in `_drain_shadow_clone_inbox` + `routing_meta` captured before `await` so mid-drain mutations are impossible
- **C2** — all gateway DB access uses `connect_closing()` context manager; no connection leaks
- **C3** — kanban I/O in `_drain_shadow_clone_inbox` wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread()` so SQLite never blocks the event loop
- **C4** — `_drain_completion_notifications` gains a shadow_clone routing branch that enqueues and drains completed events

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS shadow_clone_tasks (
    delegation_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    session_key      TEXT NOT NULL,
    goal             TEXT,
    kanban_ticket_id TEXT,
    routing_meta     TEXT,  -- JSON
    status           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',
    result_json      TEXT,
    dispatched_at    REAL,
    completed_at     REAL
);
```

Migration safety: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + existing `SessionDB._reconcile_columns` handles old DBs without the table.

## Tests

30 new tests in `tests/tools/test_shadow_clone_sqlite_persistence.py`; 0 regressions on 47 existing shadow_clone + async_delegation tests.

items.title: Native image_input_mode silently drops user images on long-lived/threaded sessions (session-key handoff mismatch); text mode works

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

With `agent.image_input_mode: native` (or `auto` resolving to native), user-attached images on a **live gateway conversation** are not delivered to the main model: the gateway logs `Image routing: native ... 1 image(s) will be attached inline`, but the model behaves as if no image was sent (asks for the missing info / says it cannot see an image). Switching to `image_input_mode: text` (vision_analyze) works perfectly, and the *same* image + model + credential works when sent through the model directly. So the model, the image format, and the credential are all fine — the image is being dropped inside the gateway's native-attach handoff.

### Environment

- Hermes 0.16.0
- Main model: `anthropic` / `claude-opus-4-8`, `base_url: https://api.anthropic.com`, auth via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (`auth_type: oauth`)
- `agent.image_input_mode: auto` (resolves to `native` because models.dev reports image input support)
- Long-lived multi-turn channel session (Slack), tool-using turns, replies within a thread

### What I verified (isolation)

Sent the exact downloaded image through `agent.auxiliary_client.async_call_llm` on the same box, same model, same OAuth credential, two ways:

| User-message image format | Result |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI-style `image_url` content part (what native mode builds) | ✅ model read it correctly |
| Anthropic-native `image` block | ✅ model read it correctly |

So `image_url` delivery, the OAuth subscription token, and `claude-opus-4-8` vision all work. `image_input_mode: text` also works end to end. Only the **gateway native conversation path** fails.

### Suspected root cause (session-key handoff mismatch)

The native handoff stashes image paths keyed by session, then pops them at the run site:

- **SET** — `gateway/run.py` ~`8054`, inside `_prepare_inbound_message_text`, keyed by `self._session_key_for_source(source)`:
  ```python
  pending_native[session_key] = list(image_paths)
  ```
- **CONSUME** — `gateway/run.py` ~`15246`, keyed by `session_entry.session_key`:
  ```python
  _native_imgs = self._consume_pending_native_image_paths(session_key)
  ```
- helper (`~8249`): `return list(pending_native.pop(session_key, []) or [])`

`_session_key_for_source()` calls `session_store._generate_session_key(source)`, whereas the run path uses `session_entry.session_key` from `get_or_create_session(source)`. For sessions that have undergone compression-continuation healing or thread-anchor resolution (the run path explicitly walks the compression-continuation chain forward to its tip), these two keys can differ. When they do, `pop(session_key, [])` returns `[]`, the image is silently dropped, and the model receives a text-only turn — even though the gateway already logged `attached inline`.

This matches the observed behavior exactly: fails on a busy, long-lived, reply-threaded channel; succeeds in a fresh isolated call; unaffected by `text` mode (which never touches this handoff).

### Steps to reproduce

1. `anthropic` / `claude-opus-4-8` as main model, `image_input_mode: auto` (or `native`).
2. Use a long-lived channel session that has gone through at least one compression-continuation (or send the image as a reply within a thread).
3. Send an image. Observe `Image routing: native ... attached inline` in the log, but the model responds as if no image was attached.
4. Set `image_input_mode: text` and repeat → the model sees the image.

### Workaround

`agent.image_input_mode: text` (routes via `vision_analyze`, bypassing the native session-keyed handoff).

### Ask

Could the SET and CONSUME sites be made to use the *same* resolved session key (e.g., key the pending-native map by the finalized `session_entry.session_key`, or consume by `_session_key_for_source(source)`), so the handoff survives compression-continuation / thread-anchor remapping? Happy to test a patch.

## Description

In the Hermes Desktop app composer (chat input), the `/` (slash command) popover triggers when `/` appears **after any whitespace**, not just at the very start of the input. This causes the user's normal text to be consumed by the command popover when typing natural content that uses `/` as a separator (e.g., Chinese text with `/`, file paths, `A/B test`, etc.).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop app
2. Type any text followed by a space and then `/` (e.g., `不附加文件 /文件夾`)
3. The slash command popover opens immediately after typing `/`
4. Text after the `/` gets interpreted as a command query
5. The user's original message content appears to disappear or gets corrupted

## Root Cause

The trigger regex in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/text-utils.ts`:

```ts
const SLASH_TRIGGER_RE = /(?:^|[\s])(\/)((?:[a-zA-Z][\w-]*(?:\s+\S*)*)?)$/
```

The `(?:^|[\s])` group matches **both** start-of-input **and** whitespace-before-/`. This means any `/` preceded by a space character triggers the slash popover. It should only trigger when `/` is the very first character of the input.

## Expected Behavior

The slash command popover should only appear when `/` is typed at the **beginning of the input** (first character, no leading whitespace). A `/` in the middle of text (even after a space) should be treated as regular content.

## Suggested Fix

Change `(?:^|[\s])` to `^` in `SLASH_TRIGGER_RE`:

```ts
const SLASH_TRIGGER_RE = /^(\/)((?:[a-zA-Z][\w-]*(?:\s+\S*)*)?)$/
```

## Environment
- Hermes Desktop (Electron) on Windows 10
- File: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/text-utils.ts`

items.title: perf(dashboard): /api/sessions/stats fetches 10 000 full session rows to count by source -- O(N) to O(1) fix available

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

`GET /api/sessions/stats` is O(N) on the session count -- it calls `db.list_sessions_rich(limit=10000, include_archived=True)` and iterates every row to build a `by_source` histogram, even though `sessions.source` is already indexed. On a large local state.db this single endpoint takes **~575-700 ms** on every Sessions page load, and because the FastAPI handler runs synchronously it head-of-line blocks all concurrent dashboard requests.

## Root Cause

`web_server.py` -- `get_session_stats()` (around line 6736):

```python
for s in db.list_sessions_rich(limit=10000, include_archived=True):
    src = str(s.get("source") or "cli")
    by_source[src] = by_source.get(src, 0) + 1
```

`list_sessions_rich` runs **two correlated subqueries per row** (preview text + `MAX(messages.timestamp)`). Fetching 10 000 rows x 2 subqueries = ~575 ms on a 3 GB `state.db` with ~15 000 sessions and ~240 000 messages.

The fix is a single SQL aggregate query -- `sessions.source` already has an index (`idx_sessions_source`):

```sql
SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY source
```

This returns in **< 1 ms** regardless of database size.

## Secondary Issue in the Same Endpoint

| Issue | Cost |
|---|---|
| `session_count(archived_only=True/False)` -- no index on `archived` -> full table scan | ~15 ms x 3 calls = ~45 ms |

Adding `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_archived ON sessions(archived)` to `SCHEMA_SQL` eliminates those scans at zero migration cost (SQLite `IF NOT EXISTS`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Hermes with a non-trivial `state.db` (>= 5 000 sessions).
2. Start `hermes dashboard`.
3. Open the Sessions page.
4. Profile `/api/sessions/stats` in browser DevTools network tab -- observe ~500-700 ms response time.
5. Verify: `SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY source` runs in < 1 ms.

## Timings (15 499 sessions, 240 929 messages, ~3 GB state.db)

| Call | Time |
|---|---|
| `list_sessions_rich(limit=10000)` -- current stats endpoint | **~575 ms** |
| `SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY source` -- proposed fix | **< 1 ms** |
| `session_count(archived=0)` -- full table scan | ~15 ms |
| `session_count(archived=0)` with `idx_sessions_archived` | ~1 ms |

## Expected Behavior

`/api/sessions/stats` responds in < 5 ms on any realistic local database.

## Proposed Fix

1. **`web_server.py` -- `get_session_stats()`**: replace the `list_sessions_rich` loop with a direct SQL `GROUP BY source` query (or a new `SessionDB.session_count_by_source()` helper).
2. **`hermes_state.py` -- `SCHEMA_SQL`**: add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_archived ON sessions(archived)` so `session_count(archived_only=True/False)` stops scanning the full table.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (current main)
- Python 3.11
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- `state.db`: 15 499 sessions, 240 929 messages, ~3 GB

items.title: [Bug]: Non-streaming Anthropic calls (compaction/aux) fail against streaming-only Anthropic-compatible endpoints

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
**Bug Description**
> When `api_mode: anthropic_messages` points at an Anthropic-*compatible* endpoint that only supports SSE (i.e. it always responds with `content-type: text/event-stream` and ignores `"stream": false`), the auxiliary/compaction code paths break. The main agent turn works because it uses `messages.stream()`, but context compression and the auxiliary client call the **non-streaming** `client.messages.create()`, which the Anthropic SDK expects to return `application/json`. Against an SSE-only endpoint the SDK hands back the raw event-stream text as a bare `str`, and the caller then crashes with `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'content'`.
>
> Such endpoints are increasingly common — internal/corporate model gateways and reverse proxies that front the Messages API frequently implement streaming only. The main loop is already streaming-only in practice, so making the few remaining `create()` calls aggregate a stream would make Hermes fully compatible with them, and is a no-op for native `api.anthropic.com`.

**Steps to Reproduce**
> 1. Configure an Anthropic-compatible provider whose `/v1/messages` always returns `text/event-stream` regardless of the `stream` field (any SSE-only relay/proxy reproduces it).
> 2. `model.api_mode: anthropic_messages`, `model.base_url: <that endpoint>`.
> 3. Run a `hermes chat` session long enough to trigger **context compression** (or any auxiliary task — title generation, triage, etc.).
> 4. The main turns stream fine, but the compaction/aux call raises.
>
> Minimal repro of the underlying SDK behavior (no Hermes needed):
> ```python
> import anthropic
> c = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="...", base_url="https://<sse-only-endpoint>")
> m = c.messages.create(model="<m>", max_tokens=16,
>                       messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
> print(type(m))            # -> <class 'str'>  (raw SSE text, not a Message)
> # m.content  -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'content'
>
> with c.messages.stream(model="<m>", max_tokens=16,
>                        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) as s:
>     print(type(s.get_final_message()))   # -> Message  (works)
> ```

**Expected Behavior**
> Auxiliary and compaction calls succeed against streaming-only Anthropic-compatible endpoints, the same way the main agent loop does. A streaming-only upstream should be fully usable.

**Actual Behavior**
> The non-streaming `messages.create()` returns SSE text as a `str`; the caller raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'content'`, breaking context compression (and any auxiliary-model task) mid-session.

**Affected Component**
> Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

**Messaging Platform**
> N/A (CLI only)

**Debug Report**
> Omitted intentionally: this is a code-level bug reproducible with any SSE-only Anthropic-compatible endpoint, and `hermes debug share` would upload a private endpoint URL + key. Root cause and a fix are below; happy to provide a redacted report if needed.

**Operating System:** macOS 15 (Darwin 25.x) — provider-independent, not OS-specific
**Python Version:** 3.11
**Hermes Version:** 0.16.0 *(confirm with `hermes version`)*

**Root Cause Analysis**
> The Anthropic SDK has two response paths: `messages.stream()` consumes SSE, while `messages.create()` expects a single JSON body. The main loop already streams (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, `_call_anthropic` → `messages.stream(...).get_final_message()`), so it's compatible. But two paths still use non-streaming `create()`:
>
> 1. `run_agent.py` → `AIAgent._anthropic_messages_create()` — the last line `return self._anthropic_client.messages.create(**api_kwargs)`. This is reached by context compaction (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, the `_anthropic_messages_create(_ant_kw)` summary/retry calls) **and** by the reactive non-streaming fallback path (`agent/conversation_loop.py`, when `_disable_streaming` is set).
> 2. `agent/auxiliary_client.py` (~L1044) → `response = self._client.messages.create(**anthropic_kwargs)` — title generation, triage, decomposer, curator, etc.
>
> Against a `text/event-stream`-only endpoint, `create()` cannot parse the body and returns a `str`, so downstream `.content` / `normalize_response()` access fails.

**Proposed Fix**
> Aggregate via the SDK's stream helper at those two sites — `messages.stream(...).get_final_message()` returns a `Message` (verified to correctly reassemble text, `tool_use` inputs, `stop_reason`, and `usage`), and is exactly what the main loop already does. It's behavior-preserving for native Anthropic and other `anthropic_messages` providers (Anthropic itself recommends streaming for long requests), and unblocks SSE-only ones.
>
> ```diff
> # run_agent.py — AIAgent._anthropic_messages_create()
> -        return self._anthropic_client.messages.create(**api_kwargs)
> +        # Some Anthropic-compatible gateways are streaming-only and never
> +        # honor non-streaming requests; aggregate the stream instead. This
> +        # matches the main turn path and is a no-op for native Anthropic.
> +        api_kwargs.pop("stream", None)
> +        with self._anthropic_client.messages.stream(**api_kwargs) as _stream:
> +            return _stream.get_final_message()
> ```
> ```diff
> # agent/auxiliary_client.py (~L1044)
> -        response = self._client.messages.create(**anthropic_kwargs)
> +        anthropic_kwargs.pop("stream", None)
> +        with self._client.messages.stream(**anthropic_kwargs) as _stream:
> +            response = _stream.get_final_message()
> ```
>
> `get_final_message()` yields a `Message`/`ParsedMessage`, so `normalize_response()` and the compaction callers are unchanged. If you'd prefer to limit blast radius, this could be gated behind a profile flag (e.g. `ProviderProfile.streaming_only`) or a base_url heuristic, but unconditional aggregation keeps it consistent with the main loop. Happy to send a PR either way.

**Are you willing to submit a PR for this?**

items.body:
## Summary

Standing `/goal` state stops working after **auto-compression** rotates the agent `session_id`. The gateway continuation queue fix (#28649) is separate; it does not move `goal:<sid>` in `state_meta`.

## What happens

1. User sets `/goal` on a gateway session (Telegram, etc.). Goal JSON is stored under `goal:<session_id>` (`hermes_cli/goals.py`, `load_goal` / `save_goal`).
2. Context hits the compression threshold. `compress_context()` in `agent/conversation_compression.py` ends the old session, allocates a **new** `session_id`, and sets `parent_session_id` on the new row.
3. The gateway updates `session_entry.session_id` from the agent result (`gateway/run.py`, post-turn block around the compression ordering comment).
4. `_post_turn_goal_continuation` builds `GoalManager(session_id=new_id)`. `load_goal(new_id)` returns **None** because the blob still lives on `goal:old_id`.
5. `mgr.is_active()` is false. The loop stops with no loud error. `/goal status` looks empty on the live session.

`load_goal()` does not walk `parent_session_id`. `get_compression_tip()` helps `/resume` find the live session row; it does not copy goal meta.

## This was fixed once, then reverted

Commit `4a080b1d5` (#23530) forwarded `goal:old` → `goal:new` inside `run_agent._compress_context`.

Commit `3e7145e0b` (#23813) reverted that stack (subgoal/checklist rollback). Compression logic later moved into `agent/conversation_compression.py`; the forward block was not re-added on `main`.

## Suggested fix

After `create_session(..., parent_session_id=old_session_id)` in `compress_context()`, copy the meta row when present:

```python
_goal_meta_key_old = f"goal:{old_session_id}"
_goal_meta_key_new = f"goal:{agent.session_id}"
_goal_blob = agent._session_db.get_meta(_goal_meta_key_old)
if _goal_blob:
    agent._session_db.set_meta(_goal_meta_key_new, _goal_blob)
```

Same idea as #23530, at the current rotation site. A regression test (goal active → forced compress → `GoalManager(new_sid).is_active()` still true) would lock it in.

## Repro (gateway)

1. Start a long gateway chat, `/goal` with a multi-step task.
2. Drive enough tokens to trigger auto-compression (or use whatever manual compress path you have in tests).
3. Let the post-turn goal hook run on the new session id.
4. Observe: no continuation turns; goal meta missing for the new `session_id`.

## Environment

Seen on Hermes Agent v0.16.x, `main` through `3ca0ef7e` (June 2026). Running a local copy of the forward block in `conversation_compression.py` until upstream picks it up again.

Related: #28649 (continuation enqueue timing — fixed on main).

## Summary

In `agent/image_routing.py`, `decide_image_input_mode()` checks `_explicit_aux_vision_override(cfg)` **before** checking whether the main model supports vision. When a user has configured an explicit `auxiliary.vision.provider` (e.g. `google`/`gemini-2.5-flash` as a fallback for text-only models), this forces `text` mode unconditionally, even when the main model is itself vision-capable (e.g. `gpt-5.5`, Claude with vision).

The code comment says: "An explicit override means the user *wants* the text pipeline (they're paying for a dedicated vision model)."

This is too rigid. The user may want **both**: native vision when the main model supports it, and the explicit aux provider as a fallback when it doesn't.

## Current behavior (`auto` mode)

```python
if _explicit_aux_vision_override(cfg):
    return "text"           # <-- forced here, native never tried

supports = _lookup_supports_vision(provider, model, cfg)
if supports is True:
    return "native"
return "text"
```

| Main model | Explicit aux configured | Result |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.5 (vision-capable) | yes (google/gemini) | `text` — Gemini describes, gpt-5.5 never sees pixels |
| gpt-5.5 (vision-capable) | no (auto) | `native` — gpt-5.5 sees pixels directly |
| glm-5.2 (text-only) | yes (google/gemini) | `text` — Gemini describes (works) |
| glm-5.2 (text-only) | no (auto) | `text` → aggregator fallback → often None (broken) |

## Proposed fix

Reorder the check so native vision capability is evaluated **first**:

```python
supports = _lookup_supports_vision(provider, model, cfg)
if supports is True:
    return "native"
return "text"   # text mode uses resolve_vision_provider_client,
                # which already honors the explicit provider config
```

| Main model | Explicit aux configured | Result after fix |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.5 (vision-capable) | yes (google/gemini) | `native` — gpt-5.5 sees pixels (Gemini not invoked) |
| gpt-5.5 (vision-capable) | no (auto) | `native` (unchanged) |
| glm-5.2 (text-only) | yes (google/gemini) | `text` — Gemini describes (unchanged) |
| glm-5.2 (text-only) | no (auto) | `text` → aggregator fallback (unchanged) |

The `resolve_vision_provider_client` function already handles the explicit provider correctly when in `text` mode — it's only `decide_image_input_mode` that's blocking native.

## Related issues

- #29135 — image auto-routing cannot use native vision when auxiliary.vision is configured as fallback
- #47153 — hermes doctor vision warning false-positives for vision-capable main models
